   114→def _ensure_mlflow() -> bool:
   115→    """Ensure MLflow tracking is configured in the current thread.
   116→
   117→    Uses one experiment per day (protocol-processing-YYYYMMDD) so all runs
   118→    and workers share the same experiment in the MLflow UI.
   119→
   120→    Returns False immediately (no network calls) when MLflow circuit breaker
   121→    is open. On failure, trips the circuit breaker so downstream code
   122→    (tracing, middleware) immediately switches to no-ops.
   123→    """
   124→    from shared.resilience import mlflow_breaker, mlflow_is_available
   125→
   126→    if not mlflow_is_available():
   127→        return False
   128→
   129→    try:
   130→        import mlflow
   131→
   132→        tracking_uri = os.getenv("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI")
   133→        if tracking_uri:
   134→            mlflow.set_tracking_uri(tracking_uri)
   135→            client = mlflow.MlflowClient()
   136→
   137→            # Restore the Default experiment (id "0") if deleted.
   138→            try:
   139→                default_exp = client.get_experiment("0")
   140→                if default_exp and default_exp.lifecycle_stage == "deleted":
   141→                    client.restore_experiment("0")
   142→            except Exception:
   143→                # Non-fatal: default experiment restore is best-effort
   144→                logger.debug(
   145→                    "Could not restore default MLflow experiment",
   146→                    exc_info=True,
   147→                )
   148→
   149→            experiment_name = _get_experiment_name()
   150→            try:
   151→                mlflow.set_experiment(experiment_name)
   152→            except mlflow.exceptions.MlflowException:
   153→                # Experiment in deleted state — restore and reuse.
   154→                exp = client.get_experiment_by_name(experiment_name)
   155→                if exp and exp.lifecycle_stage == "deleted":
   156→                    client.restore_experiment(exp.experiment_id)
   157→                    mlflow.set_experiment(experiment_name)
   158→                else:
   159→                    raise
   160→            return True
   161→    except ImportError:
   162→        logger.warning("mlflow not installed — tracing disabled")
   163→    except Exception:
   164→        logger.warning("MLflow setup failed — tracing disabled", exc_info=True)
   165→        # Trip breaker so downstream code immediately uses no-ops
   166→        try:
   167→            mlflow_breaker.open()
   168→        except Exception:
   169→            pass
   170→    return False

   173→def _is_auth_expired_error(e: BaseException) -> bool:
   174→    """Return True if the exception is or was caused by credential refresh failure.
   175→
   176→    Checks the exception and its __cause__ chain so gRPC-wrapped RefreshErrors
   177→    are detected. Used to avoid retries and to raise AuthExpiredError for the outbox.
   178→    """
   179→    try:
   180→        from google.auth.exceptions import RefreshError
   181→    except ImportError:
   182→        return False
   183→    exc: BaseException | None = e
   184→    while exc is not None:
   185→        if isinstance(exc, RefreshError):
   186→            return True
   187→        exc = getattr(exc, "__cause__", None)
   188→    return False
   189→
   190→
   191→def _categorize_pipeline_error(e: Exception) -> str:
   192→    """Convert exception to human-readable pipeline error reason.
   193→
   194→    Combines extraction and grounding error categorization from both
   195→    the old extraction_service and grounding_service triggers.
   196→
   197→    Args:
   198→        e: The exception that occurred during pipeline execution.
   199→
   200→    Returns:
   201→        Human-readable error message for the user.
   202→    """
   203→    if isinstance(e, DependencyCheckError):
   204→        return f"Infrastructure dependency unavailable: {e}"
   205→
   206→    error_str = str(e).lower()
   207→
   208→    # PDF / extraction errors
   209→    if "pdf" in error_str or "pymupdf" in error_str:
   210→        return "PDF text quality too low or file corrupted"
   211→    if "gcs" in error_str or "storage" in error_str or "bucket" in error_str:
   212→        return "File storage service unavailable"
   213→
   214→    # Auth / credential errors (do not retry — trigger login in UI)
   215→    if "credential" in error_str or "auth" in error_str or "refresherror" in error_str:
   216→        return "Google credentials expired — sign in again"
   217→
   218→    # UMLS / grounding errors
   219→    if "mcp" in error_str or "subprocess" in error_str:
   220→        return "UMLS grounding service unavailable"
   221→    if "concept_linking" in error_str or "concept_search" in error_str:
   222→        return "UMLS terminology service unavailable"
   223→
   224→    # Generic transient errors
   225→    if "circuit" in error_str:
   226→        return "AI service temporarily unavailable"
   227→    if "timeout" in error_str or "timed out" in error_str:
   228→        return "Processing timed out"
   229→    if "parse" in error_str:
   230→        return "Protocol parsing failed"
   231→
   232→    return f"Pipeline failed: {type(e).__name__}"
   233→
   234→
   235→def _update_protocol_failed(
   236→    protocol_id: str,
   237→    reason: str,
   238→    error_category: str,
   239→    exception_type: str,
   240→) -> None:
   241→    """Update protocol status to extraction_failed with error metadata.
   242→
   243→    Args:
   244→        protocol_id: Protocol ID to update.
   245→        reason: Human-readable error reason.
   246→        error_category: Short category string for the error type.
   247→        exception_type: Python exception class name.
   248→    """
   249→    try:
   250→        with Session(engine) as session:
   251→            protocol = session.get(Protocol, protocol_id)
   252→            if protocol:
   253→                protocol.status = "extraction_failed"
   254→                protocol.error_reason = reason
   255→                protocol.metadata_ = {
   256→                    **protocol.metadata_,
   257→                    "error": {
   258→                        "category": error_category,
   259→                        "reason": reason,
   260→                        "exception_type": exception_type,
   261→                    },
   262→                }
   263→                session.add(protocol)
   264→                session.commit()
   265→    except Exception:
   266→        logger.exception(
   267→            "Failed to update protocol %s status to extraction_failed",
   268→            protocol_id,
   269→        )

   272→async def _run_pipeline(
   273→    initial_state: dict[str, Any],
   274→    config: dict[str, Any],
   275→    payload: dict[str, Any],
   276→) -> dict[str, Any]:
   277→    """Run the pipeline graph with MLflow tracing inside the async context.
   278→
   279→    MLflow ContextVars must be created in the same async context as the
   280→    LangGraph invocation. asyncio.run() creates an isolated context, so
   281→    we initialize MLflow tracing HERE (inside asyncio.run) rather than
   282→    in the sync caller.
   283→
   284→    Each pipeline node creates its own separate MLflow trace tagged with
   285→    protocol_id and run_id, so traces appear in the MLflow UI as they
   286→    complete rather than waiting for the entire pipeline. Filter by the
   287→    run_id tag to see all traces from a single pipeline invocation.
   288→    """
   289→    from protocol_processor.graph import get_graph
   290→    from protocol_processor.tracing import set_pipeline_run_id
   291→
   292→    graph = await get_graph()
   293→
   294→    # MLflow tracing: do NOT enable langchain.autolog() here.
   295→    # Autolog wraps the entire ainvoke() in a single trace that only
   296→    # appears in MLflow after the full pipeline completes.  Instead,
   297→    # each node creates its own independent trace via pipeline_span()
   298→    # so traces appear in real-time as nodes finish.
   299→    # MLflow for this thread is set by handle_protocol_uploaded() via
   300→    # _ensure_mlflow() (protocol-processing-YYYYMMDD). Do not call
   301→    # _ensure_mlflow() again here.
   302→
   303→    # Set run_id so every node's pipeline_span() tags its trace with the
   304→    # same identifier.  Uses the thread_id which is "{protocol_id}:{uuid4}".
   305→    thread_id = config.get("configurable", {}).get("thread_id", "")
   306→    if thread_id:
   307→        set_pipeline_run_id(thread_id)
   308→
   309→    state: dict[str, Any] = await graph.ainvoke(initial_state, config)
   310→    return state
   311→

   313→class DependencyCheckError(RuntimeError):
   314→    """Raised when a required infrastructure dependency is unreachable."""
   315→
   316→
   317→def _preflight_check() -> None:
   318→    """Verify infrastructure dependencies are reachable before starting the pipeline.
   319→
   320→    Checks: PostgreSQL (main DB) and OMOP vocabulary DB as hard dependencies.
   321→    MLflow tracking server is checked as a soft dependency -- pipeline proceeds
   322→    with tracing disabled if MLflow is unreachable.
   323→
   324→    Raises DependencyCheckError only for DB or OMOP failures so the pipeline
   325→    never starts without core infrastructure.
   326→    """
   327→    import urllib.request
   328→
   329→    from sqlalchemy import text
   330→
   331→    # 1. Main database (required for persist, parse, etc.)
   332→    try:
   333→        with engine.connect() as conn:
   334→            conn.execute(text("SELECT 1"))
   335→    except Exception as exc:
   336→        raise DependencyCheckError(
   337→            f"Main database (DATABASE_URL) is not reachable: {exc}"
   338→        ) from exc
   339→
   340→    # 2. OMOP vocabulary database (required for dual grounding)
   341→    try:
   342→        from protocol_processor.tools.omop_mapper import _get_omop_engine
   343→
   344→        omop_engine = _get_omop_engine()
   345→        with omop_engine.connect() as conn:
   346→            conn.execute(text("SELECT 1"))
   347→    except Exception as exc:
   348→        raise DependencyCheckError(
   349→            f"OMOP vocabulary database (OMOP_VOCAB_URL) is not reachable: {exc}"
   350→        ) from exc
   351→
   352→    logger.info("Pre-flight checks passed: DB, OMOP reachable")
   353→
   354→    # 3. MLflow tracking server (soft dependency -- tracing only)
   355→    from shared.resilience import mlflow_breaker
   356→
   357→    tracking_uri = os.getenv("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI")
   358→    if not tracking_uri:
   359→        logger.info("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI not set - tracing disabled")
   360→        return
   361→
   362→    # Refresh Cloud Run ID token for service-to-service auth
   363→    try:
   364→        from api_service._cloud_run_auth import configure_mlflow_auth
   365→
   366→        configure_mlflow_auth()
   367→    except Exception:
   368→        logger.debug("Cloud Run MLflow auth refresh skipped", exc_info=True)
   369→
   370→    try:
   371→        req = urllib.request.Request(f"{tracking_uri}/health", method="GET")
   372→        # Add auth header if we have a token (Cloud Run service-to-service)
   373→        token = os.getenv("MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN")
   374→        if token:
   375→            req.add_header("Authorization", f"Bearer {token}")
   376→        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=5) as resp:
   377→            if resp.status >= 400:
   378→                logger.warning(
   379→                    "MLflow health check returned HTTP %d - tracing disabled",
   380→                    resp.status,
   381→                )
   382→                mlflow_breaker.open()
   383→                return
   384→        logger.info("Pre-flight: MLflow reachable at %s", tracking_uri)
   385→    except Exception:
   386→        logger.warning(
   387→            "MLflow unreachable at %s - tracing disabled for this pipeline run",
   388→            tracking_uri,
   389→        )
   390→        # Trip breaker immediately so all MLflow operations become no-ops
   391→        try:
   392→            mlflow_breaker.open()
   393→        except Exception:
   394→            pass
   395→
   396→
   397→def handle_protocol_uploaded(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   398→    """Handle a ProtocolUploaded event by running the full pipeline.
   399→
   400→    Constructs the initial PipelineState from the event payload and
   401→    invokes the consolidated 5-node LangGraph workflow via asyncio.run().
   402→
   403→    Uses protocol_id as the LangGraph thread_id so that retry_from_checkpoint
   404→    can locate the saved checkpoint by protocol_id alone.
   405→
   406→    Replaces both extraction_service.trigger.handle_protocol_uploaded and
   407→    grounding_service.trigger.handle_criteria_extracted from the v1.x
   408→    two-service architecture.
   409→
   410→    Args:
   411→        payload: Event payload dict containing protocol_id, file_uri, and title.
   412→
   413→    Raises:
   414→        DependencyCheckError: If DB or OMOP is unreachable.
   415→        Exception: Re-raised after logging to let the outbox processor
   416→            mark the event as failed for retry.
   417→    """
   418→    # Pre-flight: verify all infrastructure dependencies are up before
   419→    # spending any Gemini/ToolUniverse API calls.
   420→    _preflight_check()
   421→
   422→    # Set MLflow experiment for this worker thread (protocol-processing-YYYYMMDD).
   423→    # Without this, the thread would use default experiment ID 0, which may be deleted.
   424→    _ensure_mlflow()
   425→    # So pipeline spans carry the experiment ID and export works from any thread.
   426→    try:
   427→        import mlflow
   428→
   429→        from protocol_processor.tracing import set_pipeline_experiment_id
   430→
   431→        exp = mlflow.get_experiment_by_name(_get_experiment_name())
   432→        if exp:
   433→            set_pipeline_experiment_id(exp.experiment_id)
   434→        else:
   435→            set_pipeline_experiment_id(None)
   436→    except Exception:
   437→        logger.debug("Could not set pipeline experiment ID for tracing", exc_info=True)
   438→
   439→    protocol_id = payload.get("protocol_id", "unknown")
   440→    logger.info(
   441→        "Handling ProtocolUploaded event for protocol %s (consolidated pipeline)",
   442→        protocol_id,
   443→    )
   444→
   445→    try:
   446→        # Generate unique thread_id per pipeline run to prevent checkpoint collision
   447→        # on re-extraction (same protocol_id would resume old completed checkpoint)
   448→        thread_id = f"{protocol_id}:{uuid4()}"
   449→
   450→        initial_state: dict[str, Any] = {
   451→            "protocol_id": payload["protocol_id"],
   452→            "file_uri": payload["file_uri"],
   453→            "title": payload["title"],
   454→            "batch_id": None,
   455→            "pdf_bytes": None,
   456→            "extraction_json": None,
   457→            "entities_json": None,
   458→            "grounded_entities_json": None,
   459→            "archived_reviewed_criteria": payload.get("archived_reviewed_criteria"),
   460→            "status": "processing",
   461→            "error": None,
   462→            "errors": [],
   463→        }
   464→
   465→        # Store thread_id in protocol metadata for retry_from_checkpoint lookup
   466→        try:
   467→            with Session(engine) as session:
   468→                protocol = session.get(Protocol, protocol_id)
   469→                if protocol:
   470→                    meta = protocol.metadata_ or {}
   471→                    protocol.metadata_ = {
   472→                        **meta,
   473→                        "pipeline_thread_id": thread_id,
   474→                    }
   475→                    session.add(protocol)
   476→                    session.commit()
   477→        except Exception:
   478→            logger.warning(
   479→                "Failed to store pipeline_thread_id for protocol %s",
   480→                protocol_id,
   481→            )
   482→
   483→        config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": thread_id}}
   484→
   485→        asyncio.run(_run_pipeline(initial_state, config, payload))
   486→
   487→        logger.info(
   488→            "Protocol pipeline completed for protocol %s",
   489→            protocol_id,
   490→        )
   491→
   492→    except Exception as e:
   493→        logger.exception(
   494→            "Protocol pipeline failed for protocol %s",
   495→            protocol_id,
   496→        )
   497→        reason = _categorize_pipeline_error(e)
   498→        # Auth expiry: do not retry; outbox marks dead_letter, UI shows login.
   499→        is_auth_expired = _is_auth_expired_error(e)
   500→        category = "auth_expired" if is_auth_expired else "pipeline_failed"
   501→        _update_protocol_failed(
   502→            protocol_id,
   503→            reason,
   504→            category,
   505→            type(e).__name__,
   506→        )
   507→        if is_auth_expired:
   508→            raise AuthExpiredError("Google credentials expired — sign in again") from e
   509→        raise
   510→
   511→
   512→async def retry_from_checkpoint(protocol_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
   513→    """Resume pipeline from last checkpoint for a failed protocol.
   514→
   515→    Passes None as the input state to graph.ainvoke, which tells LangGraph
   516→    to resume from the last saved checkpoint for the given thread_id instead
   517→    of starting from scratch. Reads thread_id from protocol.metadata_ where
   518→    it was stored during the original pipeline invocation.
   519→
   520→    Args:
   521→        protocol_id: Protocol ID — used to look up thread_id from metadata.
   522→
   523→    Returns:
   524→        Final pipeline state dict after resuming from checkpoint.
   525→    """
   526→    with Session(engine) as session:
   527→        protocol = session.get(Protocol, protocol_id)
   528→        if not protocol:
   529→            raise ValueError(f"Protocol {protocol_id} not found")
   530→        thread_id = (protocol.metadata_ or {}).get("pipeline_thread_id", protocol_id)
   531→
   532→    from protocol_processor.graph import get_graph
   533→
   534→    graph = await get_graph()
   535→    config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": thread_id}}
   536→    # Pass None as input — LangGraph resumes from last checkpoint
   537→    result: dict[str, Any] = await graph.ainvoke(None, config)
   538→    return result

**Mode:** standard

**Project State:**
Phase 1 complete (MLflow Decoupling - circuit breaker, async trace logging, middleware gating).
Phase 2 next: Service Auth and MLflow Recovery.

**Roadmap:**
### Phase 2: Service Auth and MLflow Recovery
**Goal**: MLflow Cloud Run service accepts authenticated requests from the API, and tokens stay fresh across the service lifetime
**Depends on**: Phase 1
**Requirements**: AUTH-01, AUTH-02
**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
  1. The API can write trace data to the MLflow Cloud Run service using ID tokens obtained from the metadata server (no 403 errors)
  2. After the API has been running for more than 1 hour, MLflow trace exports still succeed (token is refreshed before expiry)

**Phase requirement IDs (every ID MUST appear in a plan's `requirements` field):** AUTH-01, AUTH-02

**Requirements:**
- AUTH-01: MLflow Cloud Run service accepts authenticated requests from API service (ID token via metadata server)
- AUTH-02: MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN is refreshed before each pipeline run (not just at startup)

**Phase Context:**
IMPORTANT: Context contains USER DECISIONS from /gsd:discuss-phase.
- **Decisions** = LOCKED — honor exactly, do not revisit
- **Claude's Discretion** = Freedom — make implementation choices
- **Deferred Ideas** = Out of scope — do NOT include

### Token refresh strategy (LOCKED)
- Lazy refresh on expiry: check token age before use, refresh only if expired or within 10-minute buffer
- Cloud Run ID tokens last ~1 hour; refresh when ≤10 minutes remain before expiry
- If metadata server is unreachable during refresh: skip MLflow entirely (trip circuit breaker)
- Token refresh should integrate with the existing `_cloud_run_auth.py` module

### Claude's Discretion
- Keep --allow-unauthenticated on MLflow (research recommends this)
- Integrate failure with Phase 1 circuit breaker (research recommends this)
- Keep existing module-level token cache pattern (research recommends this)
- Defer RequestAuthProvider plugin to v2

**Research:**
Read the file: .REDACTED.md

Key findings from research:
1. MLflow is deployed with --allow-unauthenticated, so 403s are from cold-start/503, not IAM
2. Existing _cloud_run_auth.py is architecturally correct, needs 3 small changes:
   - Update _TOKEN_REFRESH_MARGIN from 300 to 600 (10 min)
   - Call configure_mlflow_auth() from middleware's _get_mlflow_if_ready()
   - Trip mlflow_breaker on metadata server failure
3. No new dependencies needed
4. Non-MLflow auth blockers should be verified (OAuth callback, GCS signing, CORS)
</planning_context>

1→"""Shared resilience patterns: circuit breakers and retry helpers.
     2→
     3→Per-service circuit breakers for GCS, Gemini, UMLS MCP, Vertex AI, and MLflow.
     4→Each breaker trips after 3 consecutive failures (per CONTEXT.md decision)
     5→and recovers after 60 seconds (Claude's discretion), except MLflow which
     6→uses a 120-second recovery timeout (per user decision).
     7→"""
     8→
     9→import logging
    10→import os
    11→
    12→from pybreaker import (
    13→    CircuitBreaker,
    14→    CircuitBreakerListener,
    15→    CircuitBreakerState,
    16→)
    17→
    18→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    19→
    20→# Recovery timeout: 60 seconds per research recommendation
    21→_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT = 60
    22→# MLflow recovery timeout: 120 seconds per user decision (separate from other breakers)
    23→_MLFLOW_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT = 120
    24→# Failure threshold: 3 consecutive failures per CONTEXT.md decision
    25→_FAIL_MAX = 3
    26→
    27→
    28→class MLflowCircuitBreakerListener(CircuitBreakerListener):
    29→    """Log circuit breaker state changes to MLflow.
    30→
    31→    Records when breakers trip (open), recover (half_open -> closed),
    32→    or probe (half_open). Safe no-op if MLflow unavailable.
    33→
    34→    Special case: when the mlflow breaker itself changes state, log only to
    35→    the Python logger (avoid recursion — can't log to MLflow if MLflow is down).
    36→    This also implements the user decision for "log a single warning when it
    37→    goes down, then suppress until recovery" since pybreaker fires state_change
    38→    once per transition.
    39→    """
    40→
    41→    def state_change(
    42→        self,
    43→        cb: CircuitBreaker,
    44→        old_state: CircuitBreakerState | None,
    45→        new_state: CircuitBreakerState,
    46→    ) -> None:
    47→        """Handle circuit breaker state change by logging to MLflow or Python logger."""
    48→        # MLflow breaker: log to Python logger only (avoid recursion)
    49→        if cb.name == "mlflow":
    50→            if new_state == CircuitBreakerState.OPEN:
    51→                logger.warning(
    52→                    "MLflow circuit breaker OPEN - tracing disabled until recovery"
    53→                )
    54→            elif new_state == CircuitBreakerState.HALF_OPEN:
    55→                logger.info(
    56→                    "MLflow circuit breaker probing - attempting recovery"
    57→                )
    58→            elif new_state == CircuitBreakerState.CLOSED:
    59→                logger.info("MLflow circuit breaker CLOSED - tracing resumed")
    60→            return
    61→
    62→        # Other breakers: log to MLflow
    63→        try:
    64→            import mlflow
    65→
    66→            tracking_uri = os.getenv("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI")
    67→            if not tracking_uri:
    68→                return
    69→
    70→            with mlflow.start_span(
    71→                name=f"circuit_breaker_{cb.name}",
    72→                span_type="TOOL",
    73→            ) as span:
    74→                span.set_inputs(
    75→                    {
    76→                        "service": cb.name,
    77→                        "old_state": str(old_state),
    78→                        "new_state": str(new_state),
    79→                        "fail_counter": cb.fail_counter,
    80→                    }
    81→                )
    82→        except Exception:
    83→            logger.debug("MLflow circuit breaker logging failed", exc_info=True)
    84→
    85→
    86→# Create listener instance
    87→_mlflow_listener = MLflowCircuitBreakerListener()
    88→
    89→gemini_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
    90→    fail_max=_FAIL_MAX,
    91→    reset_timeout=_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT,
    92→    name="gemini",
    93→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
    94→)
    95→
    96→umls_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
    97→    fail_max=_FAIL_MAX,
    98→    reset_timeout=_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT,
    99→    name="umls",
   100→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
   101→)
   102→
   103→gcs_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
   104→    fail_max=_FAIL_MAX,
   105→    reset_timeout=_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT,
   106→    name="gcs",
   107→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
   108→)
   109→
   110→vertex_ai_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
   111→    fail_max=_FAIL_MAX,
   112→    reset_timeout=_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT,
   113→    name="vertex_ai",
   114→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
   115→)
   116→
   117→# ToolUniverse circuit breaker — higher fail threshold (10 vs 3) because
   118→# ToolUniverse wraps multiple APIs and transient failures are more common.
   119→# fail_max=10 per user decision (NOT reusing _FAIL_MAX=3 from other breakers).
   120→tu_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
   121→    fail_max=10,
   122→    reset_timeout=60,
   123→    name="tooluniverse",
   124→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
   125→)
   126→
   127→# MLflow circuit breaker — 2-minute recovery timeout per user decision.
   128→# Prevents repeated connection attempts to unreachable MLflow server.
   129→# All MLflow operations (tracing, middleware, init) check this breaker.
   130→mlflow_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
   131→    fail_max=_FAIL_MAX,
   132→    reset_timeout=_MLFLOW_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT,
   133→    name="mlflow",
   134→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
   135→)
   136→
   137→
   138→def mlflow_is_available() -> bool:
   139→    """Check if MLflow circuit breaker allows operations.
   140→
   141→    Returns True when the breaker is closed (healthy) or half-open (probing).
   142→    Returns False when the breaker is open (MLflow known to be down).
   143→    """
   144→    return str(mlflow_breaker.current_state) != "open"
   145→

# Roadmap: MedGemma Deployment Fix

## Overview

All three deployment failures (MLflow 403/503, API unresponsive, dead-lettered protocols) trace to a single root cause: MLflow treated as a hard dependency. Phase 1 decouples MLflow so the pipeline runs regardless of MLflow health. Phase 2 fixes service-to-service auth so MLflow tracing works when MLflow IS available. Phase 3 hardens the deploy script with probes, CPU config, validation, and post-deploy verification. After all three phases, the full protocol upload-to-export pipeline runs reliably on Cloud Run with graceful MLflow degradation.

## Phases

**Phase Numbering:**
- Integer phases (1, 2, 3): Planned milestone work
- Decimal phases (2.1, 2.2): Urgent insertions (marked with INSERTED)

Decimal phases appear between their surrounding integers in numeric order.

- [x] **Phase 1: MLflow Decoupling** - Make MLflow optional so the pipeline and API work regardless of MLflow health
- [ ] **Phase 2: Service Auth and MLflow Recovery** - Fix service-to-service auth so MLflow tracing works when available
- [ ] **Phase 3: Deploy Hardening** - Make deploy script robust, self-verifying, and production-ready

## Phase Details

### Phase 1: MLflow Decoupling
**Goal**: Protocol processing and API responsiveness work regardless of MLflow health status
**Depends on**: Nothing (first phase)
**Requirements**: MLFL-01, MLFL-02, MLFL-03, MLFL-04, LOCL-01, LOCL-02
**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
  1. A protocol PDF uploaded via the API completes the full 7-node extraction pipeline when MLflow is unreachable (no dead-lettering)
  2. The API /health endpoint responds within 2 seconds even when MLflow is returning 503 on every request
  3. When MLflow comes back online after being down, tracing resumes automatically without restarting the API
  4. Running the full pipeline locally via Docker Compose produces identical results to before these changes (no regressions)
**Plans**: 2 plans

Plans:
- [x] 01-01-PLAN.md — Add MLflow circuit breaker, convert preflight to soft warning, harden init
- [x] 01-02-PLAN.md — Gate tracing/middleware with breaker, health endpoint, async trace logging config

### Phase 2: Service Auth and MLflow Recovery
**Goal**: MLflow Cloud Run service accepts authenticated requests from the API, and tokens stay fresh across the service lifetime
**Depends on**: Phase 1
**Requirements**: AUTH-01, AUTH-02
**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
  1. The API can write trace data to the MLflow Cloud Run service using ID tokens obtained from the metadata server (no 403 errors)
  2. After the API has been running for more than 1 hour, MLflow trace exports still succeed (token is refreshed before expiry)
**Plans**: 1 plan

Plans:
- [ ] 02-01-PLAN.md — Update token refresh margin to 10 min, trip circuit breaker on auth failure, wire refresh into middleware

### Phase 3: Deploy Hardening
**Goal**: Deploy script is robust, idempotent, and self-verifying so deployments succeed reliably without manual intervention
**Depends on**: Phase 1
**Requirements**: DEPL-01, DEPL-02, DEPL-03, DEPL-04
**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
  1. Running the deploy script with a missing required env var fails immediately with a clear error message (before any gcloud commands execute)
  2. The deployed API container starts successfully under Cloud Run's startup probe without false-positive restarts
  3. The outbox background processor continues polling for pending protocols between HTTP requests (CPU not throttled)
  4. After deploy completes, the script automatically verifies the new revision is healthy and reports pass/fail
**Plans**: TBD

Plans:
- [ ] 03-01: TBD

## Progress

**Execution Order:**
Phases execute in numeric order: 1 -> 2 -> 3

| Phase | Plans Complete | Status | Completed |
|-------|----------------|--------|-----------|
| 1. MLflow Decoupling | 2/2 | Complete | 2026-02-27 |
| 2. Service Auth and MLflow Recovery | 0/1 | In Progress | - |
| 3. Deploy Hardening | 0/0 | Not started | - |

1→"""Helpers for Cloud Run service-to-service authentication.
     2→
     3→On Cloud Run, services behind IAM require an ID token for invocation.
     4→This module fetches ID tokens from the metadata server and configures
     5→MLflow to use them via MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN.
     6→"""
     7→
     8→from __future__ import annotations
     9→
    10→import logging
    11→import os
    12→import threading
    13→import time
    14→
    15→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    16→
    17→# Cache token and its expiry to avoid hitting metadata server on every call.
    18→_token_lock = threading.Lock()
    19→_cached_token: str | None = None
    20→_token_expiry: float = 0.0  # epoch seconds
    21→_TOKEN_REFRESH_MARGIN = 300  # refresh 5 min before expiry
    22→
    23→
    24→def _is_cloud_run() -> bool:
    25→    """Check if we're running on Cloud Run."""
    26→    return bool(os.getenv("K_SERVICE"))
    27→
    28→
    29→def get_id_token(audience: str) -> str | None:
    30→    """Fetch an ID token for the given audience from the metadata server.
    31→
    32→    Returns None if not running on Cloud Run or if the fetch fails.
    33→    Caches the token and refreshes it when close to expiry.
    34→    """
    35→    global _cached_token, _token_expiry  # noqa: PLW0603
    36→
    37→    if not _is_cloud_run():
    38→        return None
    39→
    40→    with _token_lock:
    41→        now = time.time()
    42→        if _cached_token and now < _token_expiry - _TOKEN_REFRESH_MARGIN:
    43→            return _cached_token
    44→
    45→        try:
    46→            import requests as _requests
    47→
    48→            resp = _requests.get(
    49→                "http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/"
    50→                f"instance/service-accounts/default/identity?audience={audience}",
    51→                headers={"Metadata-Flavor": "Google"},
    52→                timeout=3,
    53→            )
    54→            resp.raise_for_status()
    55→            token = resp.text.strip()
    56→
    57→            # ID tokens from metadata server are valid for ~1 hour
    58→            _cached_token = token
    59→            _token_expiry = now + 3600
    60→            logger.info("Fetched Cloud Run ID token for audience: %s", audience)
    61→            return token
    62→        except Exception:
    63→            logger.warning(
    64→                "Could not fetch ID token for %s from metadata server",
    65→                audience,
    66→                exc_info=True,
    67→            )
    68→            return None
    69→
    70→
    71→def configure_mlflow_auth() -> None:
    72→    """Set MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN for Cloud Run service-to-service auth.
    73→
    74→    Must be called before any MLflow client operations. Safe to call
    75→    multiple times -- refreshes the token if needed.
    76→    """
    77→    tracking_uri = os.getenv("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI")
    78→    if not tracking_uri or not _is_cloud_run():
    79→        return
    80→
    81→    token = get_id_token(tracking_uri)
    82→    if token:
    83→        os.environ["MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN"] = token
    84→        logger.info("Set MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN for Cloud Run auth")
    85→

1→"""MLflow request tracing middleware for FastAPI.
     2→
     3→Uses a pure ASGI middleware instead of Starlette's BaseHTTPMiddleware to
     4→preserve contextvars propagation (required for MLflow tracing).
     5→BaseHTTPMiddleware runs call_next in a thread pool, which breaks
     6→contextvars and produces malformed trace spans.
     7→"""
     8→
     9→import logging
    10→import os
    11→import time
    12→from typing import Any
    13→
    14→from shared.resilience import mlflow_breaker, mlflow_is_available
    15→from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Message, Receive, Scope, Send
    16→
    17→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    18→
    19→# Skip tracing for health/readiness probes
    20→_SKIP_PATHS = {"/health", "/ready", "/"}
    21→
    22→
    23→def _get_mlflow_if_ready(path: str) -> Any | None:
    24→    """Return the mlflow module if tracing should be applied, else None.
    25→
    26→    Checks are ordered cheapest-first: path skip, circuit breaker, env var,
    27→    then import.  Returns None (skip tracing) on any check failure.
    28→    """
    29→    if path in _SKIP_PATHS:
    30→        return None
    31→    if not mlflow_is_available():
    32→        return None
    33→    if not os.getenv("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI"):
    34→        return None
    35→    try:
    36→        import mlflow
    37→
    38→        return mlflow
    39→    except ImportError:
    40→        return None
    41→
    42→
    43→class MLflowRequestMiddleware:
    44→    """Pure ASGI middleware that creates MLflow traces for API requests."""
    45→
    46→    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp) -> None:
    47→        """Store the ASGI app to call."""
    48→        self.app = app
    49→
    50→    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
    51→        """Handle request and optionally wrap it in an MLflow span."""
    52→        if scope["type"] != "http":
    53→            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
    54→            return
    55→
    56→        path = scope.get("path", "")
    57→        mlflow = _get_mlflow_if_ready(path)
    58→        if mlflow is None:
    59→            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
    60→            return
    61→
    62→        method = scope.get("method", "?")
    63→        start = time.perf_counter()
    64→        status_code = 500  # default until we see the actual response
    65→
    66→        # Capture status code from response headers
    67→        async def send_wrapper(message: Message) -> None:
    68→            nonlocal status_code
    69→            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
    70→                status_code = message.get("status", 500)
    71→            await send(message)
    72→
    73→        app_called = False
    74→        try:
    75→            with mlflow.start_span(
    76→                name=f"{method} {path}",
    77→                span_type="HTTP",
    78→            ) as span:
    79→                query = scope.get("query_string", b"").decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    80→                span.set_inputs({"method": method, "path": path, "query": query})
    81→
    82→                app_called = True
    83→                await self.app(scope, receive, send_wrapper)
    84→                latency_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
    85→
    86→                span.set_outputs(
    87→                    {
    88→                        "status_code": status_code,
    89→                        "latency_ms": round(latency_ms, 2),
    90→                    }
    91→                )
    92→        except Exception:
    93→            logger.warning(
    94→                "MLflow request tracing failed, continuing without trace",
    95→                exc_info=True,
    96→            )
    97→            # Trip breaker so subsequent requests skip MLflow immediately
    98→            try:
    99→                mlflow_breaker.open()
   100→            except Exception:
   101→                pass
   102→            if not app_called:
   103→                await self.app(scope, receive, send)
   104→

   117→### Pattern 1: Lazy Token Refresh Before Use
   118→**What:** Check token age before every MLflow operation. Refresh only when expired or within buffer.
   119→**When to use:** Every code path that uses MLflow (middleware, pipeline trigger, init).
   120→**Example:**
   121→```python
   122→# In _cloud_run_auth.py
   123→_TOKEN_REFRESH_MARGIN = 600  # 10 minutes per user decision (was 5)
   124→
   125→def configure_mlflow_auth() -> None:
   126→    """Refresh MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN if close to expiry.
   127→
   128→    Safe to call on every request -- no-ops when token is still fresh.
   129→    Trips mlflow_breaker on metadata server failure.
   130→    """
   131→    tracking_uri = os.getenv("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI")
   132→    if not tracking_uri or not _is_cloud_run():
   133→        return
   134→
   135→    token = get_id_token(tracking_uri)
   136→    if token:
   137→        os.environ["MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN"] = token
   138→    else:
   139→        # Metadata server unreachable -- trip breaker
   140→        from shared.resilience import mlflow_breaker
   141→        try:
   142→            mlflow_breaker.open()
   143→        except Exception:
   144→            pass
   145→```
   146→
   147→### Pattern 2: Token Refresh Integrated with Middleware
   148→**What:** Call `configure_mlflow_auth()` from `_get_mlflow_if_ready()` before creating spans.
   149→**When to use:** MLflow request middleware, before any mlflow.start_span() call.
   150→**Example:**
   151→```python
   152→# In middleware.py
   153→def _get_mlflow_if_ready(path: str) -> Any | None:
   154→    if path in _SKIP_PATHS:
   155→        return None
   156→    if not mlflow_is_available():
   157→        return None
   158→    if not os.getenv("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI"):
   159→        return None
   160→
   161→    # Refresh token if needed (no-op when fresh or not on Cloud Run)
   162→    try:
   163→        from api_service._cloud_run_auth import configure_mlflow_auth
   164→        configure_mlflow_auth()
   165→    except Exception:
   166→        pass  # Token refresh failure handled by configure_mlflow_auth
   167→
   168→    try:
   169→        import mlflow
   170→        return mlflow
   171→    except ImportError:
   172→        return None
   173→```

   175→### Anti-Patterns to Avoid
   176→- **Background timer thread for token refresh:** Adds complexity for no benefit. Lazy refresh on use is simpler and achieves the same result. A dedicated refresh thread would also need its own error handling, shutdown logic, and circuit breaker integration. The user decided on lazy refresh -- do not add a timer.
   177→- **Clearing MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI on auth failure:** This would prevent recovery. The token is separate from the URI. The circuit breaker gates access; the URI must stay set.
   178→- **Decoding the JWT to check `exp` claim:** The existing approach of tracking `_token_expiry = now + 3600` is simpler and avoids import dependencies. JWT decoding is unnecessarily complex for this use case.
   179→- **Retrying token refresh in the hot path:** If metadata server is unreachable, trip the breaker immediately. Do not add retry loops to the middleware request path.

   189→2. Switching to `--no-allow-unauthenticated` requires: (a) identifying the API service's service account, (b) granting `roles/run.invoker`, (c) ensuring the token refresh works perfectly, and (d) verifying the entire flow end-to-end. This adds risk for a hackathon project.

This means token refresh happens automatically per-request without needing to set environment variables. But it requires creating a separate installable package with entry_points, which is overkill for this phase.
   252→
   253→### Non-MLflow Auth/Permission Issues: Flag for Verification
   254→
   255→**Recommendation:** During implementation, verify the end-to-end flow and fix any blockers found.
   256→
   257→**Potential blockers identified from codebase analysis:**

On Cloud Run behind a proxy, this could generate `http://` instead of `https://`. The `ProxyHeadersMiddleware` (main.py line 198) should fix this, but it needs `X-Forwarded-Proto` from the load balancer. **Verify in production.**

   267→## Don't Hand-Roll
   268→
   269→| Problem | Don't Build | Use Instead | Why |
   270→|---------|-------------|-------------|-----|
   271→| Token cache with thread safety | Custom cache class | Existing `_token_lock` + `_cached_token` pattern in `_cloud_run_auth.py` | Already works, already thread-safe, user said extend it |

   275→
   276→**Key insight:** The existing code in `_cloud_run_auth.py` is architecturally correct. It just needs three small fixes: (1) update the refresh margin from 5 to 10 minutes, (2) call it from the middleware, and (3) trip the circuit breaker on failure.
   277→
   278→## Common Pitfalls
   279→
   280→### Pitfall 1: MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN Set But MLflow Server Does Not Require Auth
   281→**What goes wrong:** Setting `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN` when MLflow is deployed with `--allow-unauthenticated`. The token is sent as a Bearer header, but the MLflow server (v2.19.0 without `--app-name basic-auth`) ignores it. This is harmless but confusing -- it makes it look like auth is working when it is actually not enforced.
   282→**Why it happens:** Cloud Run IAM auth and MLflow built-in auth are separate layers. `--allow-unauthenticated` disables Cloud Run's IAM check. MLflow's built-in auth (`--app-name basic-auth`) is a separate feature that must be explicitly enabled.
   283→**How to avoid:** Understand the two layers. Document that the current setup uses `--allow-unauthenticated` (Cloud Run ignores IAM) and no MLflow built-in auth (server ignores tokens). The token is present for future IAM restriction.
   284→**Warning signs:** Auth "works" even with an expired or bogus token -- because nobody is checking it.
   285→
   286→### Pitfall 2: Token Refresh in Middleware Adds Latency to Every Request
   287→**What goes wrong:** Calling `configure_mlflow_auth()` on every HTTP request could add metadata server latency to every request.
   288→**Why it happens:** The metadata server call takes 5-50ms. If called on every request, this accumulates.
   289→**How to avoid:** The existing lazy cache in `get_id_token()` already prevents this. The function checks `now < _token_expiry - _TOKEN_REFRESH_MARGIN` and returns the cached token immediately (0ms) for 50+ minutes of every hour. The metadata server is only called once when the cache expires. This pattern is safe for the hot path.
   290→**Warning signs:** None expected. The metadata server call only happens once per ~50 minutes.
   291→
   292→### Pitfall 3: Race Condition in Token Refresh Across Threads
   293→**What goes wrong:** Two threads call `configure_mlflow_auth()` simultaneously when the token is expired. Both enter the lock, but only one refreshes. The second thread might read a stale `os.environ["MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN"]` if it was read before the first thread's write.
   294→**Why it happens:** `os.environ` is not atomic with the lock in `_cloud_run_auth.py`.
   295→**How to avoid:** The existing `_token_lock` already serializes access. The second thread will see the fresh `_cached_token` when it enters the lock. The `os.environ` write happens inside the lock. This is already correct. No additional synchronization needed.
   296→**Warning signs:** This pitfall does NOT apply to the current code -- it is already handled.
   297→
   298→### Pitfall 4: MLflow v2.19.0 Server vs v3.x Client API Mismatch
   299→**What goes wrong:** The server runs MLflow v2.19.0 (from `infra/mlflow/Dockerfile`). The client uses MLflow >=3.8.1 (from `pyproject.toml` dev deps). API compatibility issues may surface.
   300→**Why it happens:** MLflow v3.x client can write to v2.x servers, but some features (like `search_traces`, `MlflowExperimentLocation`) may not be available on the server side.
   301→**How to avoid:** This is explicitly deferred per user decision (MLflow version alignment is out of scope). The Phase 1 circuit breaker handles API errors gracefully. Do NOT attempt to fix version mismatch in this phase.
   302→**Warning signs:** `AttributeError` or `MlflowException` when calling v3-only APIs.
   303→
   304→### Pitfall 5: Metadata Server Unavailable Locally
   305→**What goes wrong:** Running the app locally (not on Cloud Run), `get_id_token()` tries to reach `metadata.google.internal` which does not exist. This takes up to the 3-second timeout before returning None.
   306→**Why it happens:** `_is_cloud_run()` checks `K_SERVICE` env var, which correctly gates the metadata server call. But if someone accidentally sets `K_SERVICE` locally, the timeout would apply.
   307→**How to avoid:** The guard is already correct. `_is_cloud_run()` returns False locally. No code changes needed for LOCL-01/LOCL-02 compliance (verified in Phase 1 research).
   308→**Warning signs:** 3-second delays at startup or per-request when running locally with K_SERVICE set.

1→"""Shared resilience patterns: circuit breakers and retry helpers.
     2→
     3→Per-service circuit breakers for GCS, Gemini, UMLS MCP, Vertex AI, and MLflow.
     4→Each breaker trips after 3 consecutive failures (per CONTEXT.md decision)
     5→and recovers after 60 seconds (Claude's discretion), except MLflow which
     6→uses a 120-second recovery timeout (per user decision).
     7→"""
     8→
     9→import logging
    10→import os
    11→
    12→from pybreaker import (
    13→    CircuitBreaker,
    14→    CircuitBreakerListener,
    15→    CircuitBreakerState,
    16→)
    17→
    18→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    19→
    20→# Recovery timeout: 60 seconds per research recommendation
    21→_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT = 60
    22→# MLflow recovery timeout: 120 seconds per user decision (separate from other breakers)
    23→_MLFLOW_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT = 120
    24→# Failure threshold: 3 consecutive failures per CONTEXT.md decision
    25→_FAIL_MAX = 3
    26→
    27→
    28→class MLflowCircuitBreakerListener(CircuitBreakerListener):
    29→    """Log circuit breaker state changes to MLflow.
    30→
    31→    Records when breakers trip (open), recover (half_open -> closed),
    32→    or probe (half_open). Safe no-op if MLflow unavailable.
    33→
    34→    Special case: when the mlflow breaker itself changes state, log only to
    35→    the Python logger (avoid recursion — can't log to MLflow if MLflow is down).
    36→    This also implements the user decision for "log a single warning when it
    37→    goes down, then suppress until recovery" since pybreaker fires state_change
    38→    once per transition.
    39→    """
    40→
    41→    def state_change(
    42→        self,
    43→        cb: CircuitBreaker,
    44→        old_state: CircuitBreakerState | None,
    45→        new_state: CircuitBreakerState,
    46→    ) -> None:
    47→        """Handle circuit breaker state change by logging to MLflow or Python logger."""
    48→        # MLflow breaker: log to Python logger only (avoid recursion)
    49→        if cb.name == "mlflow":
    50→            if new_state == CircuitBreakerState.OPEN:
    51→                logger.warning(
    52→                    "MLflow circuit breaker OPEN - tracing disabled until recovery"
    53→                )
    54→            elif new_state == CircuitBreakerState.HALF_OPEN:
    55→                logger.info(
    56→                    "MLflow circuit breaker probing - attempting recovery"
    57→                )
    58→            elif new_state == CircuitBreakerState.CLOSED:
    59→                logger.info("MLflow circuit breaker CLOSED - tracing resumed")
    60→            return
    61→
    62→        # Other breakers: log to MLflow
    63→        try:
    64→            import mlflow
    65→
    66→            tracking_uri = os.getenv("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI")
    67→            if not tracking_uri:
    68→                return
    69→
    70→            with mlflow.start_span(
    71→                name=f"circuit_breaker_{cb.name}",
    72→                span_type="TOOL",
    73→            ) as span:
    74→                span.set_inputs(
    75→                    {
    76→                        "service": cb.name,
    77→                        "old_state": str(old_state),
    78→                        "new_state": str(new_state),
    79→                        "fail_counter": cb.fail_counter,
    80→                    }
    81→                )
    82→        except Exception:
    83→            logger.debug("MLflow circuit breaker logging failed", exc_info=True)
    84→
    85→
    86→# Create listener instance
    87→_mlflow_listener = MLflowCircuitBreakerListener()
    88→
    89→gemini_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
    90→    fail_max=_FAIL_MAX,
    91→    reset_timeout=_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT,
    92→    name="gemini",
    93→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
    94→)
    95→
    96→umls_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
    97→    fail_max=_FAIL_MAX,
    98→    reset_timeout=_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT,
    99→    name="umls",
   100→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
   101→)
   102→
   103→gcs_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
   104→    fail_max=_FAIL_MAX,
   105→    reset_timeout=_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT,
   106→    name="gcs",
   107→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
   108→)
   109→
   110→vertex_ai_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
   111→    fail_max=_FAIL_MAX,
   112→    reset_timeout=_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT,
   113→    name="vertex_ai",
   114→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
   115→)
   116→
   117→# ToolUniverse circuit breaker — higher fail threshold (10 vs 3) because
   118→# ToolUniverse wraps multiple APIs and transient failures are more common.
   119→# fail_max=10 per user decision (NOT reusing _FAIL_MAX=3 from other breakers).
   120→tu_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
   121→    fail_max=10,
   122→    reset_timeout=60,
   123→    name="tooluniverse",
   124→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
   125→)
   126→
   127→# MLflow circuit breaker — 2-minute recovery timeout per user decision.
   128→# Prevents repeated connection attempts to unreachable MLflow server.
   129→# All MLflow operations (tracing, middleware, init) check this breaker.
   130→mlflow_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
   131→    fail_max=_FAIL_MAX,
   132→    reset_timeout=_MLFLOW_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT,
   133→    name="mlflow",
   134→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
   135→)
   136→
   137→
   138→def mlflow_is_available() -> bool:
   139→    """Check if MLflow circuit breaker allows operations.
   140→
   141→    Returns True when the breaker is closed (healthy) or half-open (probing).
   142→    Returns False when the breaker is open (MLflow known to be down).
   143→    """
   144→    return str(mlflow_breaker.current_state) != "open"
   145→

1→"""Helpers for Cloud Run service-to-service authentication.
     2→
     3→On Cloud Run, services behind IAM require an ID token for invocation.
     4→This module fetches ID tokens from the metadata server and configures
     5→MLflow to use them via MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN.
     6→"""
     7→
     8→from __future__ import annotations
     9→
    10→import logging
    11→import os
    12→import threading
    13→import time
    14→
    15→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    16→
    17→# Cache token and its expiry to avoid hitting metadata server on every call.
    18→_token_lock = threading.Lock()
    19→_cached_token: str | None = None
    20→_token_expiry: float = 0.0  # epoch seconds
    21→_TOKEN_REFRESH_MARGIN = 300  # refresh 5 min before expiry
    22→
    23→
    24→def _is_cloud_run() -> bool:
    25→    """Check if we're running on Cloud Run."""
    26→    return bool(os.getenv("K_SERVICE"))
    27→
    28→
    29→def get_id_token(audience: str) -> str | None:
    30→    """Fetch an ID token for the given audience from the metadata server.
    31→
    32→    Returns None if not running on Cloud Run or if the fetch fails.
    33→    Caches the token and refreshes it when close to expiry.
    34→    """
    35→    global _cached_token, _token_expiry  # noqa: PLW0603
    36→
    37→    if not _is_cloud_run():
    38→        return None
    39→
    40→    with _token_lock:
    41→        now = time.time()
    42→        if _cached_token and now < _token_expiry - _TOKEN_REFRESH_MARGIN:
    43→            return _cached_token
    44→
    45→        try:
    46→            import requests as _requests
    47→
    48→            resp = _requests.get(
    49→                "http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/"
    50→                f"instance/service-accounts/default/identity?audience={audience}",
    51→                headers={"Metadata-Flavor": "Google"},
    52→                timeout=3,
    53→            )
    54→            resp.raise_for_status()
    55→            token = resp.text.strip()
    56→
    57→            # ID tokens from metadata server are valid for ~1 hour
    58→            _cached_token = token
    59→            _token_expiry = now + 3600
    60→            logger.info("Fetched Cloud Run ID token for audience: %s", audience)
    61→            return token
    62→        except Exception:
    63→            logger.warning(
    64→                "Could not fetch ID token for %s from metadata server",
    65→                audience,
    66→                exc_info=True,
    67→            )

1→"""MLflow request tracing middleware for FastAPI.
     2→
     3→Uses a pure ASGI middleware instead of Starlette's BaseHTTPMiddleware to
     4→preserve contextvars propagation (required for MLflow tracing).
     5→BaseHTTPMiddleware runs call_next in a thread pool, which breaks
     6→contextvars and produces malformed trace spans.
     7→"""
     8→
     9→import logging
    10→import os
    11→import time
    12→from typing import Any
    13→
    14→from shared.resilience import mlflow_breaker, mlflow_is_available
    15→from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Message, Receive, Scope, Send
    16→
    17→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    18→
    19→# Skip tracing for health/readiness probes
    20→_SKIP_PATHS = {"/health", "/ready", "/"}
    21→
    22→
    23→def _get_mlflow_if_ready(path: str) -> Any | None:
    24→    """Return the mlflow module if tracing should be applied, else None.
    25→
    26→    Checks are ordered cheapest-first: path skip, circuit breaker, env var,
    27→    then import.  Returns None (skip tracing) on any check failure.
    28→    """
    29→    if path in _SKIP_PATHS:
    30→        return None
    31→    if not mlflow_is_available():
    32→        return None
    33→    if not os.getenv("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI"):
    34→        return None
    35→    try:
    36→        import mlflow
    37→
    38→        return mlflow
    39→    except ImportError:
    40→        return None
    41→
    42→
    43→class MLflowRequestMiddleware:
    44→    """Pure ASGI middleware that creates MLflow traces for API requests."""
    45→
    46→    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp) -> None:
    47→        """Store the ASGI app to call."""
    48→        self.app = app
    49→
    50→    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
    51→        """Handle request and optionally wrap it in an MLflow span."""
    52→        if scope["type"] != "http":
    53→            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
    54→            return
    55→
    56→        path = scope.get("path", "")
    57→        mlflow = _get_mlflow_if_ready(path)
    58→        if mlflow is None:
    59→            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
    60→            return
    61→
    62→        method = scope.get("method", "?")
    63→        start = time.perf_counter()
    64→        status_code = 500  # default until we see the actual response
    65→
    66→        # Capture status code from response headers
    67→        async def send_wrapper(message: Message) -> None:
    68→            nonlocal status_code
    69→            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
    70→                status_code = message.get("status", 500)
    71→            await send(message)
    72→
    73→        app_called = False
    74→        try:
    75→            with mlflow.start_span(
    76→                name=f"{method} {path}",
    77→                span_type="HTTP",
    78→            ) as span:
    79→                query = scope.get("query_string", b"").decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    80→                span.set_inputs({"method": method, "path": path, "query": query})
    81→
    82→                app_called = True
    83→                await self.app(scope, receive, send_wrapper)
    84→                latency_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
    85→
    86→                span.set_outputs(
    87→                    {
    88→                        "status_code": status_code,
    89→                        "latency_ms": round(latency_ms, 2),
    90→                    }
    91→                )
    92→        except Exception:
    93→            logger.warning(
    94→                "MLflow request tracing failed, continuing without trace",
    95→                exc_info=True,
    96→            )
    97→            # Trip breaker so subsequent requests skip MLflow immediately
    98→            try:
    99→                mlflow_breaker.open()
   100→            except Exception:
   101→                pass
   102→            if not app_called:
   103→                await self.app(scope, receive, send)
   104→

1→"""Shared resilience patterns: circuit breakers and retry helpers.
     2→
     3→Per-service circuit breakers for GCS, Gemini, UMLS MCP, Vertex AI, and MLflow.
     4→Each breaker trips after 3 consecutive failures (per CONTEXT.md decision)
     5→and recovers after 60 seconds (Claude's discretion), except MLflow which
     6→uses a 120-second recovery timeout (per user decision).
     7→"""
     8→
     9→import logging
    10→import os
    11→
    12→from pybreaker import (
    13→    CircuitBreaker,
    14→    CircuitBreakerListener,
    15→    CircuitBreakerState,
    16→)
    17→
    18→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    19→
    20→# Recovery timeout: 60 seconds per research recommendation
    21→_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT = 60
    22→# MLflow recovery timeout: 120 seconds per user decision (separate from other breakers)
    23→_MLFLOW_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT = 120
    24→# Failure threshold: 3 consecutive failures per CONTEXT.md decision
    25→_FAIL_MAX = 3
    26→
    27→
    28→class MLflowCircuitBreakerListener(CircuitBreakerListener):
    29→    """Log circuit breaker state changes to MLflow.
    30→
    31→    Records when breakers trip (open), recover (half_open -> closed),
    32→    or probe (half_open). Safe no-op if MLflow unavailable.
    33→
    34→    Special case: when the mlflow breaker itself changes state, log only to
    35→    the Python logger (avoid recursion — can't log to MLflow if MLflow is down).
    36→    This also implements the user decision for "log a single warning when it
    37→    goes down, then suppress until recovery" since pybreaker fires state_change
    38→    once per transition.
    39→    """
    40→
    41→    def state_change(
    42→        self,
    43→        cb: CircuitBreaker,
    44→        old_state: CircuitBreakerState | None,
    45→        new_state: CircuitBreakerState,
    46→    ) -> None:
    47→        """Handle circuit breaker state change by logging to MLflow or Python logger."""
    48→        # MLflow breaker: log to Python logger only (avoid recursion)
    49→        if cb.name == "mlflow":
    50→            if new_state == CircuitBreakerState.OPEN:
    51→                logger.warning(
    52→                    "MLflow circuit breaker OPEN - tracing disabled until recovery"
    53→                )
    54→            elif new_state == CircuitBreakerState.HALF_OPEN:
    55→                logger.info(
    56→                    "MLflow circuit breaker probing - attempting recovery"
    57→                )
    58→            elif new_state == CircuitBreakerState.CLOSED:
    59→                logger.info("MLflow circuit breaker CLOSED - tracing resumed")
    60→            return
    61→
    62→        # Other breakers: log to MLflow
    63→        try:
    64→            import mlflow
    65→
    66→            tracking_uri = os.getenv("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI")
    67→            if not tracking_uri:
    68→                return
    69→
    70→            with mlflow.start_span(
    71→                name=f"circuit_breaker_{cb.name}",
    72→                span_type="TOOL",
    73→            ) as span:
    74→                span.set_inputs(
    75→                    {
    76→                        "service": cb.name,
    77→                        "old_state": str(old_state),
    78→                        "new_state": str(new_state),
    79→                        "fail_counter": cb.fail_counter,
    80→                    }
    81→                )
    82→        except Exception:
    83→            logger.debug("MLflow circuit breaker logging failed", exc_info=True)
    84→
    85→
    86→# Create listener instance
    87→_mlflow_listener = MLflowCircuitBreakerListener()
    88→
    89→gemini_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
    90→    fail_max=_FAIL_MAX,
    91→    reset_timeout=_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT,
    92→    name="gemini",
    93→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
    94→)
    95→
    96→umls_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
    97→    fail_max=_FAIL_MAX,
    98→    reset_timeout=_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT,
    99→    name="umls",
   100→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
   101→)
   102→
   103→gcs_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
   104→    fail_max=_FAIL_MAX,
   105→    reset_timeout=_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT,
   106→    name="gcs",
   107→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
   108→)
   109→
   110→vertex_ai_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
   111→    fail_max=_FAIL_MAX,
   112→    reset_timeout=_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT,
   113→    name="vertex_ai",
   114→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
   115→)
   116→
   117→# ToolUniverse circuit breaker — higher fail threshold (10 vs 3) because
   118→# ToolUniverse wraps multiple APIs and transient failures are more common.
   119→# fail_max=10 per user decision (NOT reusing _FAIL_MAX=3 from other breakers).
   120→tu_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
   121→    fail_max=10,
   122→    reset_timeout=60,
   123→    name="tooluniverse",
   124→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
   125→)
   126→
   127→# MLflow circuit breaker — 2-minute recovery timeout per user decision.
   128→# Prevents repeated connection attempts to unreachable MLflow server.
   129→# All MLflow operations (tracing, middleware, init) check this breaker.
   130→mlflow_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
   131→    fail_max=_FAIL_MAX,
   132→    reset_timeout=_MLFLOW_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT,
   133→    name="mlflow",
   134→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
   135→)
   136→
   137→
   138→def mlflow_is_available() -> bool:
   139→    """Check if MLflow circuit breaker allows operations.
   140→
   141→    Returns True when the breaker is closed (healthy) or half-open (probing).
   142→    Returns False when the breaker is open (MLflow known to be down).
   143→    """
   144→    return str(mlflow_breaker.current_state) != "open"
   145→

1→"""Helpers for Cloud Run service-to-service authentication.
     2→
     3→On Cloud Run, services behind IAM require an ID token for invocation.
     4→This module fetches ID tokens from the metadata server and configures
     5→MLflow to use them via MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN.
     6→"""
     7→
     8→from __future__ import annotations
     9→
    10→import logging
    11→import os
    12→import threading
    13→import time
    14→
    15→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    16→
    17→# Cache token and its expiry to avoid hitting metadata server on every call.
    18→_token_lock = threading.Lock()
    19→_cached_token: str | None = None
    20→_token_expiry: float = 0.0  # epoch seconds
    21→_TOKEN_REFRESH_MARGIN = 600  # refresh 10 min before expiry
    22→
    23→
    24→def _is_cloud_run() -> bool:
    25→    """Check if we're running on Cloud Run."""
    26→    return bool(os.getenv("K_SERVICE"))
    27→
    28→
    29→def get_id_token(audience: str) -> str | None:
    30→    """Fetch an ID token for the given audience from the metadata server.
    31→
    32→    Returns None if not running on Cloud Run or if the fetch fails.
    33→    Caches the token and refreshes it when close to expiry.
    34→    """
    35→    global _cached_token, _token_expiry  # noqa: PLW0603
    36→
    37→    if not _is_cloud_run():
    38→        return None
    39→
    40→    with _token_lock:
    41→        now = time.time()
    42→        if _cached_token and now < _token_expiry - _TOKEN_REFRESH_MARGIN:
    43→            return _cached_token
    44→
    45→        try:
    46→            import requests as _requests
    47→
    48→            resp = _requests.get(
    49→                "http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/"
    50→                f"instance/service-accounts/default/identity?audience={audience}",
    51→                headers={"Metadata-Flavor": "Google"},
    52→                timeout=3,
    53→            )
    54→            resp.raise_for_status()
    55→            token = resp.text.strip()
    56→
    57→            # ID tokens from metadata server are valid for ~1 hour
    58→            _cached_token = token
    59→            _token_expiry = now + 3600
    60→            logger.info("Fetched Cloud Run ID token for audience: %s", audience)
    61→            return token
    62→        except Exception:
    63→            logger.warning(
    64→                "Could not fetch ID token for %s from metadata server",
    65→                audience,
    66→                exc_info=True,
    67→            )
    68→            # Trip MLflow circuit breaker -- metadata server unreachable means
    69→            # we cannot authenticate to MLflow. Skip MLflow entirely.
    70→            try:
    71→                from shared.resilience import mlflow_breaker
    72→
    73→                mlflow_breaker.open()
    74→            except Exception:
    75→                pass
    76→            return None
    77→
    78→
    79→def configure_mlflow_auth() -> None:
    80→    """Set MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN for Cloud Run service-to-service auth.
    81→
    82→    Must be called before any MLflow client operations. Safe to call
    83→    multiple times -- refreshes the token if needed.
    84→    """
    85→    tracking_uri = os.getenv("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI")
    86→    if not tracking_uri or not _is_cloud_run():
    87→        return
    88→
    89→    token = get_id_token(tracking_uri)
    90→    if token:
    91→        os.environ["MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN"] = token
    92→        logger.info("Set MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN for Cloud Run auth")
    93→

1→"""MLflow request tracing middleware for FastAPI.
     2→
     3→Uses a pure ASGI middleware instead of Starlette's BaseHTTPMiddleware to
     4→preserve contextvars propagation (required for MLflow tracing).
     5→BaseHTTPMiddleware runs call_next in a thread pool, which breaks
     6→contextvars and produces malformed trace spans.
     7→"""
     8→
     9→import logging
    10→import os
    11→import time
    12→from typing import Any
    13→
    14→from shared.resilience import mlflow_breaker, mlflow_is_available
    15→from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Message, Receive, Scope, Send
    16→
    17→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    18→
    19→# Skip tracing for health/readiness probes
    20→_SKIP_PATHS = {"/health", "/ready", "/"}
    21→
    22→
    23→def _get_mlflow_if_ready(path: str) -> Any | None:
    24→    """Return the mlflow module if tracing should be applied, else None.
    25→
    26→    Checks are ordered cheapest-first: path skip, circuit breaker, env var,
    27→    then import.  Returns None (skip tracing) on any check failure.
    28→    """
    29→    if path in _SKIP_PATHS:
    30→        return None
    31→    if not mlflow_is_available():
    32→        return None
    33→    if not os.getenv("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI"):
    34→        return None
    35→
    36→    # Refresh Cloud Run ID token if needed (no-op when fresh or not on Cloud Run)
    37→    try:
    38→        from api_service._cloud_run_auth import configure_mlflow_auth
    39→
    40→        configure_mlflow_auth()
    41→    except Exception:
    42→        pass  # Failure handled inside configure_mlflow_auth
    43→
    44→    try:
    45→        import mlflow
    46→
    47→        return mlflow
    48→    except ImportError:
    49→        return None
    50→
    51→
    52→class MLflowRequestMiddleware:
    53→    """Pure ASGI middleware that creates MLflow traces for API requests."""
    54→
    55→    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp) -> None:
    56→        """Store the ASGI app to call."""
    57→        self.app = app
    58→
    59→    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
    60→        """Handle request and optionally wrap it in an MLflow span."""
    61→        if scope["type"] != "http":
    62→            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
    63→            return
    64→
    65→        path = scope.get("path", "")
    66→        mlflow = _get_mlflow_if_ready(path)
    67→        if mlflow is None:
    68→            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
    69→            return
    70→
    71→        method = scope.get("method", "?")
    72→        start = time.perf_counter()
    73→        status_code = 500  # default until we see the actual response
    74→
    75→        # Capture status code from response headers
    76→        async def send_wrapper(message: Message) -> None:
    77→            nonlocal status_code
    78→            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
    79→                status_code = message.get("status", 500)
    80→            await send(message)
    81→
    82→        app_called = False
    83→        try:
    84→            with mlflow.start_span(
    85→                name=f"{method} {path}",
    86→                span_type="HTTP",
    87→            ) as span:
    88→                query = scope.get("query_string", b"").decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    89→                span.set_inputs({"method": method, "path": path, "query": query})
    90→
    91→                app_called = True
    92→                await self.app(scope, receive, send_wrapper)
    93→                latency_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
    94→
    95→                span.set_outputs(
    96→                    {
    97→                        "status_code": status_code,
    98→                        "latency_ms": round(latency_ms, 2),
    99→                    }
   100→                )
   101→        except Exception:
   102→            logger.warning(
   103→                "MLflow request tracing failed, continuing without trace",
   104→                exc_info=True,
   105→            )
   106→            # Trip breaker so subsequent requests skip MLflow immediately
   107→            try:
   108→                mlflow_breaker.open()
   109→            except Exception:
   110→                pass
   111→            if not app_called:
   112→                await self.app(scope, receive, send)
   113→

1→# Roadmap: MedGemma Deployment Fix
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→All three deployment failures (MLflow 403/503, API unresponsive, dead-lettered protocols) trace to a single root cause: MLflow treated as a hard dependency. Phase 1 decouples MLflow so the pipeline runs regardless of MLflow health. Phase 2 fixes service-to-service auth so MLflow tracing works when MLflow IS available. Phase 3 hardens the deploy script with probes, CPU config, validation, and post-deploy verification. After all three phases, the full protocol upload-to-export pipeline runs reliably on Cloud Run with graceful MLflow degradation.
