1→"""Shared resilience patterns: circuit breakers and retry helpers.
     2→
     3→Per-service circuit breakers for GCS, Gemini, UMLS MCP, Vertex AI, and MLflow.
     4→Each breaker trips after 3 consecutive failures (per CONTEXT.md decision)
     5→and recovers after 60 seconds (Claude's discretion), except MLflow which
     6→uses a 120-second recovery timeout (per user decision).
     7→"""
     8→
     9→import logging
    10→import os
    11→
    12→from pybreaker import (
    13→    CircuitBreaker,
    14→    CircuitBreakerListener,
    15→    CircuitBreakerState,
    16→)
    17→
    18→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    19→
    20→# Recovery timeout: 60 seconds per research recommendation
    21→_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT = 60
    22→# MLflow recovery timeout: 120 seconds per user decision (separate from other breakers)
    23→_MLFLOW_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT = 120
    24→# Failure threshold: 3 consecutive failures per CONTEXT.md decision
    25→_FAIL_MAX = 3
    26→
    27→
    28→class MLflowCircuitBreakerListener(CircuitBreakerListener):
    29→    """Log circuit breaker state changes to MLflow.
    30→
    31→    Records when breakers trip (open), recover (half_open -> closed),
    32→    or probe (half_open). Safe no-op if MLflow unavailable.
    33→
    34→    Special case: when the mlflow breaker itself changes state, log only to
    35→    the Python logger (avoid recursion — can't log to MLflow if MLflow is down).
    36→    This also implements the user decision for "log a single warning when it
    37→    goes down, then suppress until recovery" since pybreaker fires state_change
    38→    once per transition.
    39→    """
    40→
    41→    def state_change(
    42→        self,
    43→        cb: CircuitBreaker,
    44→        old_state: CircuitBreakerState | None,
    45→        new_state: CircuitBreakerState,
    46→    ) -> None:
    47→        """Handle circuit breaker state change by logging to MLflow or Python logger."""
    48→        # MLflow breaker: log to Python logger only (avoid recursion)
    49→        if cb.name == "mlflow":
    50→            if new_state == CircuitBreakerState.OPEN:
    51→                logger.warning(
    52→                    "MLflow circuit breaker OPEN - tracing disabled until recovery"
    53→                )
    54→            elif new_state == CircuitBreakerState.HALF_OPEN:
    55→                logger.info(
    56→                    "MLflow circuit breaker probing - attempting recovery"
    57→                )
    58→            elif new_state == CircuitBreakerState.CLOSED:
    59→                logger.info("MLflow circuit breaker CLOSED - tracing resumed")
    60→            return
    61→
    62→        # Other breakers: log to MLflow
    63→        try:
    64→            import mlflow
    65→
    66→            tracking_uri = os.getenv("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI")
    67→            if not tracking_uri:
    68→                return
    69→
    70→            with mlflow.start_span(
    71→                name=f"circuit_breaker_{cb.name}",
    72→                span_type="TOOL",
    73→            ) as span:
    74→                span.set_inputs(
    75→                    {
    76→                        "service": cb.name,
    77→                        "old_state": str(old_state),
    78→                        "new_state": str(new_state),
    79→                        "fail_counter": cb.fail_counter,
    80→                    }
    81→                )
    82→        except Exception:
    83→            logger.debug("MLflow circuit breaker logging failed", exc_info=True)
    84→
    85→
    86→# Create listener instance
    87→_mlflow_listener = MLflowCircuitBreakerListener()
    88→
    89→gemini_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
    90→    fail_max=_FAIL_MAX,
    91→    reset_timeout=_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT,
    92→    name="gemini",
    93→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
    94→)
    95→
    96→umls_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
    97→    fail_max=_FAIL_MAX,
    98→    reset_timeout=_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT,
    99→    name="umls",
   100→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
   101→)
   102→
   103→gcs_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
   104→    fail_max=_FAIL_MAX,
   105→    reset_timeout=_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT,
   106→    name="gcs",
   107→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
   108→)
   109→
   110→vertex_ai_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
   111→    fail_max=_FAIL_MAX,
   112→    reset_timeout=_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT,
   113→    name="vertex_ai",
   114→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
   115→)
   116→
   117→# ToolUniverse circuit breaker — higher fail threshold (10 vs 3) because
   118→# ToolUniverse wraps multiple APIs and transient failures are more common.
   119→# fail_max=10 per user decision (NOT reusing _FAIL_MAX=3 from other breakers).
   120→tu_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
   121→    fail_max=10,
   122→    reset_timeout=60,
   123→    name="tooluniverse",
   124→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
   125→)
   126→
   127→# MLflow circuit breaker — 2-minute recovery timeout per user decision.
   128→# Prevents repeated connection attempts to unreachable MLflow server.
   129→# All MLflow operations (tracing, middleware, init) check this breaker.
   130→mlflow_breaker = CircuitBreaker(
   131→    fail_max=_FAIL_MAX,
   132→    reset_timeout=_MLFLOW_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT,
   133→    name="mlflow",
   134→    listeners=[_mlflow_listener],
   135→)
   136→
   137→
   138→def mlflow_is_available() -> bool:
   139→    """Check if MLflow circuit breaker allows operations.
   140→
   141→    Returns True when the breaker is closed (healthy) or half-open (probing).
   142→    Returns False when the breaker is open (MLflow known to be down).
   143→    """
   144→    return str(mlflow_breaker.current_state) != "open"
   145→

    53→def _init_mlflow() -> None:
    54→    """Set up MLflow tracking, restoring deleted experiments if needed.
    55→
    56→    Checks MLflow circuit breaker before attempting any network calls.
    57→    Trips the breaker on failure so downstream code (middleware, tracing)
    58→    immediately switches to no-ops.
    59→    """
    60→    from shared.resilience import mlflow_breaker, mlflow_is_available
    61→
    62→    if not mlflow_is_available():
    63→        logger.info("MLflow circuit breaker open, skipping initialization")
    64→        return
    65→
    66→    try:
    67→        import mlflow
    68→    except ImportError:
    69→        logger.info("mlflow not installed, skipping initialization")
    70→        return
    71→
    72→    tracking_uri = os.getenv("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI")
    73→    if not tracking_uri:
    74→        logger.info("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI not set, skipping MLflow initialization")
    75→        return
    76→
    77→    try:
    78→        mlflow.set_tracking_uri(tracking_uri)
    79→        client = mlflow.MlflowClient()
    80→
    81→        # Restore the Default experiment (id "0") if deleted, otherwise
    82→        # traces that land before set_experiment runs will 400.
    83→        try:
    84→            default_exp = client.get_experiment("0")
    85→            if default_exp and default_exp.lifecycle_stage == "deleted":
    86→                client.restore_experiment("0")
    87→        except Exception:
    88→            # Non-fatal: default experiment restore is best-effort
    89→            logger.debug(
    90→                "Could not restore default MLflow experiment", exc_info=True
    91→            )
    92→
    93→        experiment_name = _get_experiment_name()
    94→        try:
    95→            mlflow.set_experiment(experiment_name)
    96→        except mlflow.exceptions.MlflowException:
    97→            # Experiment in deleted state — restore and reuse.
    98→            exp = client.get_experiment_by_name(experiment_name)
    99→            if exp and exp.lifecycle_stage == "deleted":
   100→                client.restore_experiment(exp.experiment_id)
   101→                mlflow.set_experiment(experiment_name)
   102→            else:
   103→                raise
   104→        # NOTE: Do NOT enable mlflow.langchain.autolog() here.
   105→        # Autolog wraps graph.ainvoke() in a single trace that only
   106→        # appears after the full pipeline finishes.  Each pipeline
   107→        # node creates its own independent trace via pipeline_span()
   108→        # so traces stream to MLflow in real-time as nodes complete.
   109→        logger.info(
   110→            "MLflow initialized: tracking_uri=%s, experiment=%s",
   111→            tracking_uri,
   112→            experiment_name,
   113→        )
   114→    except Exception:
   115→        logger.warning(
   116→            "MLflow initialization failed - tracing disabled", exc_info=True
   117→        )
   118→        # Trip breaker so middleware and tracing immediately use no-ops
   119→        try:

   121→        except Exception:

   130→    logger.info("Initializing database...")
   131→    create_db_and_tables()
   132→    logger.info("Database initialized successfully")

   141→
   142→    # Initialize MLflow in a background thread so it doesn't block startup
   143→    # (the MLflow Cloud Run service may be cold-starting, which can take 30s+)
   144→    import threading
   145→
   146→    def _deferred_mlflow_init() -> None:
   147→        try:

   149→        except Exception:

   151→            # but catch any unexpected errors to be safe.

   154→                exc_info=True,
   155→            )

   157→    mlflow_thread = threading.Thread(
   158→        target=_deferred_mlflow_init, daemon=True, name="mlflow-init"
   159→    )

   162→    # Start outbox processor as background task (skip in tests — the poll loop
   163→    # and executor shutdown add seconds of overhead per TestClient instantiation).
   164→    processor = None

   167→        # protocol_processor.trigger.handle_protocol_uploaded replaces both the
   168→        # old extraction_service.trigger and grounding_service.trigger handlers.
   169→        processor = OutboxProcessor(

   175→        task = asyncio.create_task(processor.start())
   176→        _running_tasks.add(task)

   178→
   179→    yield

   185→    # Wait for background tasks to complete
   186→    if _running_tasks:
   187→        logger.info(f"Waiting for {len(_running_tasks)} tasks to complete...")
   188→        await asyncio.gather(*_running_tasks, return_exceptions=True)

   274→def _check_omop_vocab() -> dict:
   275→    """Check OMOP vocab DB connectivity and that tables are loaded.
   276→
   277→    Returns dict with 'status' ('ok' | 'unavailable' | 'not_loaded')
   278→    and optional 'concept_count'.

   280→    omop_url = os.getenv("OMOP_VOCAB_URL")

   283→    try:

   285→        with omop_engine.connect() as conn:
   286→            row = conn.execute(text("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM concept")).scalar()
   287→            if not row or row == 0:

   289→            return {"status": "ok", "concept_count": row}

   303→    try:

#!/bin/bash
#
# Rebuild and deploy the API to Cloud Run.
# Run from repo root, or the script will cd to the repo root.
# Usage: make deploy-api  (or  bash scripts/deploy_api.sh)
# Loads environment variables from the repo root .env (GCP_PROJECT_ID, GCP_REGION,
# CONNECTION_NAME, CORS_ORIGINS, GCS_BUCKET_NAME, VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID, etc.).
#
# See DEPLOYMENT.md sections 4.2, 4.4, 4.4b for full details.

set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"

# Load .env first so all deploy variables can come from there
if [ -f "$REPO_ROOT/.env" ]; then
    set -a
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    source "$REPO_ROOT/.env"
    set +a
fi

# Apply defaults only where still unset (env / CLI override .env)
REGION="${REGION:-${GCP_REGION:-europe-west4}}"
PROJECT_ID="${PROJECT_ID:-$GCP_PROJECT_ID}"
CONNECTION_NAME="${CONNECTION_NAME:-}"
GCS_BUCKET_NAME="${GCS_BUCKET_NAME:-}"
VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID="${VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID:-}"
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID="${GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID:-}"
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET="${GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET:-}"
# Use FRONTEND_URL for deploy CORS when set (so .env can keep CORS_ORIGINS for local dev)
CORS_ORIGINS="${FRONTEND_URL:-$CORS_ORIGINS}"

if [ -z "$PROJECT_ID" ]; then
    echo "Error: PROJECT_ID not set. Set GCP_PROJECT_ID in .env or export PROJECT_ID." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Deploy requires these; set in .env or export before running
if [ -z "$CONNECTION_NAME" ]; then
    echo "Error: CONNECTION_NAME not set (Cloud SQL connection name). Set in .env or export." >&2
    exit 1
fi
if [ -z "$CORS_ORIGINS" ]; then
    echo "Error: CORS_ORIGINS not set (frontend URL). Set in .env or export." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Prefer GCS_BUCKET_NAME_PROD for deploy (local .env GCS_BUCKET_NAME may be the cloudbuild bucket)
GCS_BUCKET_NAME="${GCS_BUCKET_NAME_PROD:-${GCS_BUCKET_NAME:-${PROJECT_ID}-api-protocols}}"

if [ -z "$VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID" ]; then
    echo "Error: VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID not set. Set in .env or export." >&2
    exit 1
fi

if [ -z "$GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID" ] || [ -z "$GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET" ]; then
    echo "Warning: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET not set. Google OAuth login will be unavailable." >&2
fi

# Auto-resolve MLflow URL from Cloud Run if not explicitly set
MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI="${MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI:-}"
if [ -z "$MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI" ]; then
    MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=$(gcloud run services describe mlflow \
        --region "$REGION" --project "$PROJECT_ID" \
        --format='value(status.url)' 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI" ]; then
        echo "Auto-resolved MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI: $MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI"
    else
        echo "Warning: No MLflow service found. Protocol processing will fail without MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI." >&2
    fi
fi

cd "$REPO_ROOT"

echo "Building API image (Cloud Build)..."
gcloud builds submit \
    --project "$PROJECT_ID" \
    --config=cloudbuild-api.yaml \
    --substitutions=_REGION="${REGION}" \
    .

echo "Deploying API to Cloud Run..."
gcloud run deploy api \
    --project "$PROJECT_ID" \
    --image "${REGION}-docker.pkg.dev/${PROJECT_ID}/app-images/api:latest" \
    --region "$REGION" \
    --platform managed \
    --allow-unauthenticated \
    --add-cloudsql-instances "$CONNECTION_NAME" \
    --set-env-vars "^||^ENVIRONMENT=production||GCP_PROJECT_ID=${PROJECT_ID}||GCP_REGION=${REGION}||MODEL_BACKEND=vertex||VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID=${VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID}||GCS_BUCKET_NAME=${GCS_BUCKET_NAME}||USE_LOCAL_STORAGE=0||CORS_ORIGINS=${CORS_ORIGINS}||GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=${GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID}||GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=${GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET}||MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=${MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI}||MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASYNC_TRACE_LOGGING=true" \
    --set-secrets "DATABASE_URL=db-url:latest,SESSION_SECRET=api-session-secret:latest,JWT_SECRET_KEY=api-jwt-secret:latest,OMOP_VOCAB_URL=omop-vocab-url:latest"

echo "Done. API URL:"
gcloud run services describe api --region "$REGION" --project "$PROJECT_ID" --format='value(status.url)'

def _init_mlflow() -> None:
    """Set up MLflow tracking, restoring deleted experiments if needed.

    Checks MLflow circuit breaker before attempting any network calls.
    Trips the breaker on failure so downstream code (middleware, tracing)
    immediately switches to no-ops.
    """
    from shared.resilience import mlflow_breaker, mlflow_is_available

    if not mlflow_is_available():
        logger.info("MLflow circuit breaker open, skipping initialization")
        return

    try:
        import mlflow
    except ImportError:
        logger.info("mlflow not installed, skipping initialization")
        return

    tracking_uri = os.getenv("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI")
    if not tracking_uri:
        logger.info("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI not set, skipping MLflow initialization")
        return

    try:
        mlflow.set_tracking_uri(tracking_uri)
        client = mlflow.MlflowClient()

        # Restore the Default experiment (id "0") if deleted, otherwise
        # traces that land before set_experiment runs will 400.
        try:
            default_exp = client.get_experiment("0")
            if default_exp and default_exp.lifecycle_stage == "deleted":
                client.restore_experiment("0")
        except Exception:
            # Non-fatal: default experiment restore is best-effort
            logger.debug(
                "Could not restore default MLflow experiment", exc_info=True
            )

        experiment_name = _get_experiment_name()
        try:
            mlflow.set_experiment(experiment_name)
        except mlflow.exceptions.MlflowException:
            # Experiment in deleted state — restore and reuse.
            exp = client.get_experiment_by_name(experiment_name)
            if exp and exp.lifecycle_stage == "deleted":
                client.restore_experiment(exp.experiment_id)
                mlflow.set_experiment(experiment_name)
            else:
                raise
        # NOTE: Do NOT enable mlflow.langchain.autolog() here.
        # Autolog wraps graph.ainvoke() in a single trace that only
        # appears after the full pipeline finishes.  Each pipeline
        # node creates its own independent trace via pipeline_span()
        # so traces stream to MLflow in real-time as nodes complete.
        logger.info(
            "MLflow initialized: tracking_uri=%s, experiment=%s",
            tracking_uri,
            experiment_name,
        )
    except Exception:
        logger.warning(
            "MLflow initialization failed - tracing disabled", exc_info=True
        )
        # Trip breaker so middleware and tracing immediately use no-ops
        try:
            mlflow_breaker.open()
        except Exception:
            pass


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    """Manage the lifecycle of the FastAPI application."""
    # Startup
    logger.info("Starting up API service...")
    logger.info("Initializing database...")
    create_db_and_tables()
    logger.info("Database initialized successfully")

    # Configure Cloud Run service-to-service auth for MLflow
    try:
        from api_service._cloud_run_auth import configure_mlflow_auth

        configure_mlflow_auth()
    except Exception:
        logger.debug("Cloud Run MLflow auth setup skipped", exc_info=True)

    # Initialize MLflow in a background thread so it doesn't block startup
    # (the MLflow Cloud Run service may be cold-starting, which can take 30s+)
    import threading

    def _deferred_mlflow_init() -> None:
        try:

        except Exception:
            # _init_mlflow handles its own exceptions and trips the breaker,
            # but catch any unexpected errors to be safe.
            logger.warning(
                "MLflow initialization failed, continuing without tracing",
                exc_info=True,
            )

    mlflow_thread = threading.Thread(
        target=_deferred_mlflow_init, daemon=True, name="mlflow-init"
    )
    mlflow_thread.start()

    # Start outbox processor as background task (skip in tests — the poll loop
    # and executor shutdown add seconds of overhead per TestClient instantiation).
    processor = None
    if not os.environ.get("TESTING"):
        # Per PIPE-03: criteria_extracted outbox removed. protocol_uploaded retained.
        # protocol_processor.trigger.handle_protocol_uploaded replaces both the
        # old extraction_service.trigger and grounding_service.trigger handlers.
        processor = OutboxProcessor(
            engine=engine,
            handlers={
                "protocol_uploaded": [handle_protocol_uploaded],
            },
        )
        task = asyncio.create_task(processor.start())
        _running_tasks.add(task)
        task.add_done_callback(_running_tasks.discard)

    yield

    # Shutdown - stop outbox processor first
    if processor:
        await processor.stop()

    # Wait for background tasks to complete
    if _running_tasks:
        logger.info(f"Waiting for {len(_running_tasks)} tasks to complete...")
        await asyncio.gather(*_running_tasks, return_exceptions=True)

    engine.dispose()
    logger.info("Shutdown complete")

def _check_omop_vocab() -> dict:
    """Check OMOP vocab DB connectivity and that tables are loaded.

    Returns dict with 'status' ('ok' | 'unavailable' | 'not_loaded')
    and optional 'concept_count'.
    """
    omop_url = os.getenv("OMOP_VOCAB_URL")
    if not omop_url:
        return {"status": "unavailable", "error": "OMOP_VOCAB_URL not set"}
    try:
        omop_engine = sa_create_engine(omop_url, pool_pre_ping=True)
        with omop_engine.connect() as conn:
            row = conn.execute(text("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM concept")).scalar()
            if not row or row == 0:
                return {"status": "not_loaded", "concept_count": 0}
            return {"status": "ok", "concept_count": row}
    except Exception as e:
        return {"status": "unavailable", "error": str(e)}


def _check_gcs() -> str:
    """Check GCS connectivity and credential validity.

    Returns one of: "ok" | "auth_expired" | "unavailable" | "local_storage".
    """
    from api_service.gcs import _use_local_storage, get_bucket_name, get_gcs_client

    if _use_local_storage():
        return "local_storage"
    try:
        client = get_gcs_client()
        if client is None:
            return "unavailable"
        bucket_name = get_bucket_name()
        client.bucket(bucket_name).exists()
        return "ok"
    except Exception as e:
        try:
            from google.auth.exceptions import RefreshError

            if isinstance(e, RefreshError):
                return "auth_expired"
        except ImportError:
            pass  # google-auth not installed; skip RefreshError detection
        return "unavailable"


def _check_breakers() -> dict:
    """Return circuit breaker states as a dict."""
    from shared.resilience import gcs_breaker, gemini_breaker, vertex_ai_breaker

    return {
        "gemini": str(gemini_breaker.current_state),
        "gcs": str(gcs_breaker.current_state),
        "vertex_ai": str(vertex_ai_breaker.current_state),
    }


@app.get("/health")
async def health_check(db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    """Health check — main DB required, OMOP/GCS/breakers informational."""
    checks: dict = {}

    # Main database (required)
    try:
        db.execute(text("SELECT 1"))
        checks["database"] = "connected"
    except Exception:
        checks["database"] = "unavailable"
        return JSONResponse(
            status_code=503,
            content={"status": "not_ready", "checks": checks},
        )

    # OMOP vocabulary database (informational — doesn't block health)
    omop = _check_omop_vocab()
    checks["omop_vocab"] = omop["status"]
    if omop.get("concept_count"):
        checks["omop_concept_count"] = omop["concept_count"]

    # GCS / Google API credentials (informational)
    checks["gcs"] = _check_gcs()

    # Circuit breaker states (informational)
    checks["breakers"] = _check_breakers()

    # MLflow status (informational — does not affect health status)
    from shared.resilience import mlflow_is_available

    checks["mlflow_available"] = mlflow_is_available()

    return {"status": "healthy", "checks": checks}


@app.get("/ready")
async def readiness_check(db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    """Readiness probe — all dependencies including OMOP must be available."""
    checks: dict = {}

    try:
        db.execute(text("SELECT 1"))
        checks["database"] = "connected"
    except Exception:
        checks["database"] = "unavailable"

    omop = _check_omop_vocab()
    checks["omop_vocab"] = omop["status"]
    if omop.get("concept_count"):
        checks["omop_concept_count"] = omop["concept_count"]

    all_ok = checks["database"] == "connected" and omop["status"] == "ok"
    if not all_ok:
        return JSONResponse(
            status_code=503,
            content={"status": "not_ready", "checks": checks},
        )
    return {"status": "ready", "checks": checks}


@app.get("/")
async def root():

    return {"message": "Welcome to the API Service"}

@app.put("/local-upload/{blob_path:path}")
async def local_upload(blob_path: str, request: Request):
    """Receive a file upload and store it locally (dev mode)."""
    from api_service.gcs import local_save_file

    body = await request.body()
    try:
        local_save_file(blob_path, body)
    except ValueError:
        return JSONResponse(status_code=400, content={"detail": "Invalid file path"})
    return JSONResponse(status_code=200, content={"status": "ok"})


@app.get("/local-files/{blob_path:path}")
async def local_files(blob_path: str):
    """Serve a locally stored file (dev mode)."""
    from api_service.gcs import local_get_file_path

    try:
        file_path = local_get_file_path(blob_path)
    except ValueError:
        return JSONResponse(status_code=400, content={"detail": "Invalid file path"})
    if file_path is None:
        return JSONResponse(status_code=404, content={"detail": "File not found"})
    return FileResponse(str(file_path), media_type="application/pdf")

#!/bin/bash
#
# Deploy the latest frontend code to Cloud Run (europe-west4).
# Run from the repository root, or the script will cd to the repo root automatically.
# Usage: make deploy-frontend  (or  bash scripts/deploy_frontend.sh)
#
# Configuration is read from the repo root .env (GCP_PROJECT_ID, GCP_REGION, API_SERVICE_URL).
# Prerequisites: gcloud CLI installed and authenticated.
#
# After deploy, the live app is served at:
#   https://frontend-<PROJECT_NUMBER>.<REGION>.run.app/
#
# See DEPLOYMENT.md section 5 for full details.

set -e

# --- Repo root (script may be run from instructions/) ---
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"

# --- Configuration: defaults, then override from .env ---
REGION="${REGION:-europe-west4}"
PROJECT_ID="${PROJECT_ID:-}"
API_SERVICE_URL="${API_SERVICE_URL:-}"
BASE_PATH="${BASE_PATH:-/}"

if [ -f "$REPO_ROOT/.env" ]; then
  set -a
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  source "$REPO_ROOT/.env"
  set +a
  # Prefer GCP_* from .env for deploy
  [ -n "$GCP_PROJECT_ID" ] && PROJECT_ID="$GCP_PROJECT_ID"
  [ -n "$GCP_REGION" ] && REGION="$GCP_REGION"
  # Use API_SERVICE_URL from .env only if it looks like a real URL (not placeholder)
  if [ -n "$API_SERVICE_URL" ] && [[ "$API_SERVICE_URL" == *"XXXXX"* ]]; then
    API_SERVICE_URL=""
  fi
fi

# Env / CLI still override
REGION="${REGION:-europe-west4}"
PROJECT_ID="${PROJECT_ID:-$GCP_PROJECT_ID}"

if [ -z "$PROJECT_ID" ]; then
  echo "Error: PROJECT_ID not set. Set GCP_PROJECT_ID or PROJECT_ID in .env or export PROJECT_ID." >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "Using REGION=$REGION PROJECT_ID=$PROJECT_ID"
if [ -z "$API_SERVICE_URL" ]; then
  echo "Fetching API service URL..."
  API_SERVICE_URL="$(gcloud run services describe api --region "$REGION" --project "$PROJECT_ID" --format='value(status.url)')"
  if [ -z "$API_SERVICE_URL" ]; then
    echo "Error: Could not get API URL. Is the 'api' service deployed in $REGION? Set API_SERVICE_URL manually if needed." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "API_SERVICE_URL=$API_SERVICE_URL"
fi

cd "$REPO_ROOT"

echo "Building frontend image (Cloud Build)..."
gcloud builds submit \
  --project "$PROJECT_ID" \
  --config=cloudbuild-frontend.yaml \
  --substitutions=_VITE_API_URL="${API_SERVICE_URL}",_BASE_PATH="${BASE_PATH}",_REGION="${REGION}" \
  .

echo "Deploying frontend to Cloud Run..."
gcloud run deploy frontend \
  --project "$PROJECT_ID" \
  --image "${REGION}-docker.pkg.dev/${PROJECT_ID}/app-images/frontend:latest" \
  --region "$REGION" \
  --platform managed \
  --no-invoker-iam-check

FRONTEND_URL="$(gcloud run services describe frontend --region "$REGION" --project "$PROJECT_ID" --format='value(status.url)' 2>/dev/null)" || true
echo "Done. Frontend URL: ${FRONTEND_URL:-unknown}"

Make deploy script robust, idempotent, and self-verifying. Requirements: DEPL-01 (startup probe), DEPL-02 (--no-cpu-throttling), DEPL-03 (env var validation), DEPL-04 (post-deploy health check).

</domain>

<decisions>

### Startup probe
- Use Cloud Run startup probe pointing to /health endpoint
- Timeout: 60s initial delay, 10s period, 3 failure threshold
- /health already checks DB connectivity (returns 503 if unavailable)

### CPU throttling
- Add --no-cpu-throttling to gcloud run deploy command
- Required for outbox background processor which polls between HTTP requests
- Without this, Cloud Run throttles CPU when no requests are active, killing the outbox

### Env var validation
- Already partially done in deploy_api.sh (PROJECT_ID, CONNECTION_NAME, CORS_ORIGINS, VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID)
- Existing validation is sufficient — don't over-engineer

- After deploy completes, curl the /health endpoint and verify 200 response
- Report pass/fail to terminal
- Non-blocking: warn but don't fail the script if health check fails (new revision may need time)

- Health check retry logic (if any)
- Whether to add memory/CPU limits

- `--no-cpu-throttling` is the critical change — without it the outbox processor is dead between requests
- startup probe prevents false-positive restarts during cold start (MLflow init can take 30s+)
- Post-deploy check gives immediate confidence without manual verification

#!/bin/bash
#
# Rebuild and deploy the API to Cloud Run.
# Run from repo root, or the script will cd to the repo root.
# Usage: make deploy-api  (or  bash scripts/deploy_api.sh)
# Loads environment variables from the repo root .env (GCP_PROJECT_ID, GCP_REGION,
# CONNECTION_NAME, CORS_ORIGINS, GCS_BUCKET_NAME, VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID, etc.).
#
# See DEPLOYMENT.md sections 4.2, 4.4, 4.4b for full details.

set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"

# Load .env first so all deploy variables can come from there
if [ -f "$REPO_ROOT/.env" ]; then
    set -a
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    source "$REPO_ROOT/.env"
    set +a
fi

# Apply defaults only where still unset (env / CLI override .env)
REGION="${REGION:-${GCP_REGION:-europe-west4}}"
PROJECT_ID="${PROJECT_ID:-$GCP_PROJECT_ID}"
CONNECTION_NAME="${CONNECTION_NAME:-}"
GCS_BUCKET_NAME="${GCS_BUCKET_NAME:-}"
VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID="${VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID:-}"
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID="${GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID:-}"
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET="${GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET:-}"
# Use FRONTEND_URL for deploy CORS when set (so .env can keep CORS_ORIGINS for local dev)
CORS_ORIGINS="${FRONTEND_URL:-$CORS_ORIGINS}"

if [ -z "$PROJECT_ID" ]; then
    echo "Error: PROJECT_ID not set. Set GCP_PROJECT_ID in .env or export PROJECT_ID." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Deploy requires these; set in .env or export before running
if [ -z "$CONNECTION_NAME" ]; then
    echo "Error: CONNECTION_NAME not set (Cloud SQL connection name). Set in .env or export." >&2
    exit 1
fi
if [ -z "$CORS_ORIGINS" ]; then
    echo "Error: CORS_ORIGINS not set (frontend URL). Set in .env or export." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Prefer GCS_BUCKET_NAME_PROD for deploy (local .env GCS_BUCKET_NAME may be the cloudbuild bucket)
GCS_BUCKET_NAME="${GCS_BUCKET_NAME_PROD:-${GCS_BUCKET_NAME:-${PROJECT_ID}-api-protocols}}"

if [ -z "$VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID" ]; then
    echo "Error: VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID not set. Set in .env or export." >&2
    exit 1
fi

if [ -z "$GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID" ] || [ -z "$GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET" ]; then
    echo "Warning: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET not set. Google OAuth login will be unavailable." >&2
fi

# Auto-resolve MLflow URL from Cloud Run if not explicitly set
MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI="${MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI:-}"
if [ -z "$MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI" ]; then
    MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=$(gcloud run services describe mlflow \
        --region "$REGION" --project "$PROJECT_ID" \
        --format='value(status.url)' 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI" ]; then
        echo "Auto-resolved MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI: $MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI"
    else
        echo "Warning: No MLflow service found. Protocol processing will fail without MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI." >&2
    fi
fi

cd "$REPO_ROOT"

echo "Building API image (Cloud Build)..."
gcloud builds submit \
    --project "$PROJECT_ID" \
    --config=cloudbuild-api.yaml \
    --substitutions=_REGION="${REGION}" \
    .

echo "Deploying API to Cloud Run..."
gcloud run deploy api \
    --project "$PROJECT_ID" \
    --image "${REGION}-docker.pkg.dev/${PROJECT_ID}/app-images/api:latest" \
    --region "$REGION" \
    --platform managed \
    --allow-unauthenticated \
    --add-cloudsql-instances "$CONNECTION_NAME" \
    --set-env-vars "^||^ENVIRONMENT=production||GCP_PROJECT_ID=${PROJECT_ID}||GCP_REGION=${REGION}||MODEL_BACKEND=vertex||VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID=${VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID}||GCS_BUCKET_NAME=${GCS_BUCKET_NAME}||USE_LOCAL_STORAGE=0||CORS_ORIGINS=${CORS_ORIGINS}||GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=${GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID}||GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=${GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET}||MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=${MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI}||MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASYNC_TRACE_LOGGING=true" \
    --set-secrets "DATABASE_URL=db-url:latest,SESSION_SECRET=api-session-secret:latest,JWT_SECRET_KEY=api-jwt-secret:latest,OMOP_VOCAB_URL=omop-vocab-url:latest"

echo "Done. API URL:"
gcloud run services describe api --region "$REGION" --project "$PROJECT_ID" --format='value(status.url)'

    --region "$REGION" \

    --no-cpu-throttling \
    --add-cloudsql-instances "$CONNECTION_NAME" \
    --startup-probe-path=/health \
    --startup-probe-initial-delay=5 \
    --startup-probe-period=10 \
    --startup-probe-failure-threshold=6 \
    --set-env-vars "^||^ENVIRONMENT=production||GCP_PROJECT_ID=${PROJECT_ID}||GCP_REGION=${REGION}||MODEL_BACKEND=vertex||VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID=${VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID}||GCS_BUCKET_NAME=${GCS_BUCKET_NAME}||USE_LOCAL_STORAGE=0||CORS_ORIGINS=${CORS_ORIGINS}||GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=${GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID}||GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=${GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET}||MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=${MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI}||MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASYNC_TRACE_LOGGING=true" \
    --set-secrets "DATABASE_URL=db-url:latest,SESSION_SECRET=api-session-secret:latest,JWT_SECRET_KEY=api-jwt-secret:latest,OMOP_VOCAB_URL=omop-vocab-url:latest"

# Post-deploy health check
API_URL=$(gcloud run services describe api \
    --region "$REGION" --project "$PROJECT_ID" \
    --format='value(status.url)' 2>/dev/null)

echo "API URL: ${API_URL:-unknown}"

if [ -n "$API_URL" ]; then
    echo "Verifying deployment health..."
    HTTP_STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 30 "${API_URL}/health" 2>/dev/null || echo "000")
    if [ "$HTTP_STATUS" = "200" ]; then
        echo "Health check PASSED (HTTP $HTTP_STATUS)"
    else
        echo "Warning: Health check returned HTTP $HTTP_STATUS (new revision may still be starting)" >&2
    fi
else
    echo "Warning: Could not determine API URL for health check" >&2
fi

#!/bin/bash
#
# Rebuild and deploy the API to Cloud Run.
# Run from repo root, or the script will cd to the repo root.
# Usage: make deploy-api  (or  bash scripts/deploy_api.sh)
# Loads environment variables from the repo root .env (GCP_PROJECT_ID, GCP_REGION,
# CONNECTION_NAME, CORS_ORIGINS, GCS_BUCKET_NAME, VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID, etc.).
#
# See DEPLOYMENT.md sections 4.2, 4.4, 4.4b for full details.

set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"

# Load .env first so all deploy variables can come from there
if [ -f "$REPO_ROOT/.env" ]; then
    set -a
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    source "$REPO_ROOT/.env"
    set +a
fi

# Apply defaults only where still unset (env / CLI override .env)
REGION="${REGION:-${GCP_REGION:-europe-west4}}"
PROJECT_ID="${PROJECT_ID:-$GCP_PROJECT_ID}"
CONNECTION_NAME="${CONNECTION_NAME:-}"
GCS_BUCKET_NAME="${GCS_BUCKET_NAME:-}"
VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID="${VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID:-}"
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID="${GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID:-}"
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET="${GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET:-}"
# Use FRONTEND_URL for deploy CORS when set (so .env can keep CORS_ORIGINS for local dev)
CORS_ORIGINS="${FRONTEND_URL:-$CORS_ORIGINS}"

if [ -z "$PROJECT_ID" ]; then
    echo "Error: PROJECT_ID not set. Set GCP_PROJECT_ID in .env or export PROJECT_ID." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Deploy requires these; set in .env or export before running
if [ -z "$CONNECTION_NAME" ]; then
    echo "Error: CONNECTION_NAME not set (Cloud SQL connection name). Set in .env or export." >&2
    exit 1
fi
if [ -z "$CORS_ORIGINS" ]; then
    echo "Error: CORS_ORIGINS not set (frontend URL). Set in .env or export." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Prefer GCS_BUCKET_NAME_PROD for deploy (local .env GCS_BUCKET_NAME may be the cloudbuild bucket)
GCS_BUCKET_NAME="${GCS_BUCKET_NAME_PROD:-${GCS_BUCKET_NAME:-${PROJECT_ID}-api-protocols}}"

if [ -z "$VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID" ]; then
    echo "Error: VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID not set. Set in .env or export." >&2
    exit 1
fi

if [ -z "$GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID" ] || [ -z "$GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET" ]; then
    echo "Warning: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET not set. Google OAuth login will be unavailable." >&2
fi

# Auto-resolve MLflow URL from Cloud Run if not explicitly set
MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI="${MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI:-}"
if [ -z "$MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI" ]; then
    MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=$(gcloud run services describe mlflow \
        --region "$REGION" --project "$PROJECT_ID" \
        --format='value(status.url)' 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI" ]; then
        echo "Auto-resolved MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI: $MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI"
    else
        echo "Warning: No MLflow service found. Protocol processing will fail without MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI." >&2
    fi
fi

cd "$REPO_ROOT"

echo "Building API image (Cloud Build)..."
gcloud builds submit \
    --project "$PROJECT_ID" \
    --config=cloudbuild-api.yaml \
    --substitutions=_REGION="${REGION}" \
    .

echo "Deploying API to Cloud Run..."
gcloud run deploy api \
    --project "$PROJECT_ID" \
    --image "${REGION}-docker.pkg.dev/${PROJECT_ID}/app-images/api:latest" \
    --region "$REGION" \
    --platform managed \
    --allow-unauthenticated \
    --no-cpu-throttling \
    --add-cloudsql-instances "$CONNECTION_NAME" \
    --startup-probe-path=/health \
    --startup-probe-initial-delay=5 \
    --startup-probe-period=10 \
    --startup-probe-failure-threshold=6 \
    --set-env-vars "^||^ENVIRONMENT=production||GCP_PROJECT_ID=${PROJECT_ID}||GCP_REGION=${REGION}||MODEL_BACKEND=vertex||VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID=${VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID}||GCS_BUCKET_NAME=${GCS_BUCKET_NAME}||USE_LOCAL_STORAGE=0||CORS_ORIGINS=${CORS_ORIGINS}||GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=${GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID}||GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=${GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET}||MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=${MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI}||MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASYNC_TRACE_LOGGING=true" \
    --set-secrets "DATABASE_URL=db-url:latest,SESSION_SECRET=api-session-secret:latest,JWT_SECRET_KEY=api-jwt-secret:latest,OMOP_VOCAB_URL=omop-vocab-url:latest"

# Post-deploy health check
API_URL=$(gcloud run services describe api \
    --region "$REGION" --project "$PROJECT_ID" \
    --format='value(status.url)' 2>/dev/null)

echo "API URL: ${API_URL:-unknown}"

if [ -n "$API_URL" ]; then
    echo "Verifying deployment health..."
    HTTP_STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 30 "${API_URL}/health" 2>/dev/null || echo "000")
    if [ "$HTTP_STATUS" = "200" ]; then
        echo "Health check PASSED (HTTP $HTTP_STATUS)"
    else
        echo "Warning: Health check returned HTTP $HTTP_STATUS (new revision may still be starting)" >&2
    fi
else
    echo "Warning: Could not determine API URL for health check" >&2
fi

Now let me create a comprehensive summary of the frontend flows based on my analysis:

## Frontend App Analysis: Login Flow and Protocol Upload Flow

Based on my analysis of the `/Users/noahdolevelixir/Code/medgemma-hackathon/apps/hitl-ui` React frontend, here's what I found:

### 1. LOGIN/AUTH FLOW

**Route:** `/login`

**Auth Method:** Google OAuth (with dev login fallback)

**Flow:**
- User navigates to `/login` (LoginPage.tsx)
- Two login options:
  1. **Google OAuth** (primary): Clicks "Sign in with Google" button
     - Opens a popup to `${API_BASE_URL}/auth/login?popup=1`
     - Backend handles OAuth handshake
     - Popup sends message back to main window with `access_token` and `user` object via `postMessage`
     - Frontend listens for message and stores token in localStorage
  
  2. **Dev Login** (fallback): Available for local development only
     - POST to `${API_BASE_URL}/auth/dev-login`
     - Returns `access_token` and `user` object
     - Only works if server has dev login enabled

**Auth Storage:**
- Token: `localStorage.getItem('auth_token')` 
- User: `localStorage.getItem('auth_user')` (JSON stringified)
- Managed by Zustand store: `useAuthStore` (authStore.ts)

**Auth Headers:**
- All authenticated API calls use: `Authorization: Bearer ${token}`
- Handled by `fetchApi()` wrapper function (fetchApi.ts)

**Protected Routes:**
- RequireAuth component guards all routes except `/login`
- Redirects to `/login` if not authenticated or session expired

---

### 2. PROTOCOL UPLOAD FLOW

**Route:** `/protocols`

**Upload Dialog Component:** `ProtocolUploadDialog.tsx`

**Upload Process:**

1. **Trigger Upload:**
   - User clicks "Upload Protocol" button on ProtocolList page
   - Opens modal dialog

2. **File Selection:**
   - Accepts PDF files only (`accept="application/pdf"`)
   - Validates file type: must be `application/pdf`
   - Validates file size: max 50MB
   - Supports drag-and-drop or file picker
   - Shows file preview with name and size

3. **Upload Steps** (useUploadProtocol hook):
   - **Step 1:** POST `/protocols/upload` with metadata
     ```json
     {
       "filename": "file.name",
       "content_type": "application/pdf",
       "file_size_bytes": 12345
     }
     ```
     - Response: `{ protocol_id, upload_url, gcs_path }`
   
   - **Step 2:** PUT file directly to GCS using signed URL
     - Uses `fetch(uploadUrl, { method: 'PUT', body: file })`
     - Headers: `Content-Type: application/pdf`
   
   - **Step 3:** POST `/protocols/{protocol_id}/confirm-upload` with base64 encoded PDF
     ```json
     {
       "pdf_bytes_base64": "base64_encoded_pdf"
     }
     ```
     - Triggers quality scoring and extraction pipeline

4. **Processing States:**
   After upload, protocol goes through states:
   - `uploaded` → Initial state
   - `extracting` → PDF text/data extraction in progress
   - `extraction_failed` → Extraction error (can retry)
   - `grounding` → Entity grounding/linking in progress
   - `grounding_failed` → Grounding error (can retry)
   - `pending_review` → Ready for human review
   - `complete` → All processing done
   - `dead_letter` → Unrecoverable error (can retry)
   - `archived` → Hidden from default list

---

### 3. PROCESSING RESULTS DISPLAY

**Main Results Routes:**

1. **Protocol List Page (`/protocols`):**
   - Shows all uploaded protocols in table
   - Displays: Title, Status, Page Count, Quality Score, Upload Time
   - Filter by status or show archived
   - Status badges with color coding
   - Quality score indicator (0-100% progress bar)
   - Actions: Retry (for failed), Archive, Click to detail view

2. **Protocol Detail Page (`/protocols/:id`):**
   - Shows protocol metadata
   - Status and quality score
   - Timeline of batches/extractions
   - Agreement metrics
   - Button to "Review" (links to review batch)
   - Re-extract option (creates new batch)

3. **Review Queue (`/reviews`):**
   - Lists all review batches pending human review
   - Shows batch status, criteria count, etc.
   - Click to open ReviewPage

4. **Review Page (`/reviews/:batchId`):**
   - **Left panel:** PDF Viewer (PdfViewer.tsx) 
     - Shows original protocol PDF with page navigation
   
   - **Right panel:** Extracted criteria and entities
     - Tabs: "Criteria" and "Entities"
     - Each criterion shows:
       - Extracted text
       - Confidence score
       - Review status (approved/rejected)
       - Action buttons (Approve/Reject/Modify)
     - Entities grouped by criteria_id
   
   - **Search & Filter:**
     - Text search across criteria
     - Filter by status (pending/approved/rejected)
     - Filter by type
     - Filter by confidence level
   
   - **Audit Trail:**
     - Shows who reviewed what and when
     - Collapsible audit history panel

5. **Criteria Spreadsheet (`/criteria`):**
   - Spreadsheet view of all criteria across all batches
   - Sortable columns
   - Inline editing

6. **Entity List (`/entities/:batchId`):**
   - Lists extracted entities for a batch
   - Shows entity type and mapped values
   - Can approve/modify/reject individual entities

---

### 4. KEY API ENDPOINTS

**Authentication:**
- `POST /auth/login?popup=1` - OAuth popup login
- `POST /auth/dev-login` - Dev login

**Protocols:**
- `GET /protocols?page=1&page_size=20&status=X` - List protocols
- `GET /protocols/:id` - Get protocol detail
- `POST /protocols/upload` - Get signed upload URL
- `PUT {upload_url}` - Upload file to GCS (external)
- `POST /protocols/:id/confirm-upload` - Confirm upload and trigger processing
- `POST /protocols/:id/retry` - Retry failed protocol
- `POST /protocols/:id/re-extract` - Re-extract (new batch)
- `POST /protocols/:id/archive` - Archive protocol

**Reviews:**
- `GET /batches?page=1&page_size=X` - List review batches
- `GET /batches/:batchId/criteria` - Get criteria for batch
- `POST /criteria/:criterionId/review` - Submit criterion review
- `POST /entities/:entityId/action` - Review entity

---

### 5. PLAYWRIGHT E2E TESTING TIPS

**Login Flow for Tests:**
```javascript
// Option 1: Use dev login (faster)
await page.request.post('${API_URL}/auth/dev-login')
// Extract token from response and set in localStorage

// Option 2: Simulate OAuth popup flow
// Mock the window.postMessage from auth popup
await page.evaluate((token, user) => {
  window.dispatchEvent(new MessageEvent('message', {
    data: { access_token: token, user: user },
    origin: new URL(API_URL).origin
  }))
}, token, user)
```

**Upload Flow for Tests:**
```javascript
// 1. Get upload URL
POST /protocols/upload { filename, content_type, file_size_bytes }

// 2. Upload to GCS
PUT {upload_url} with PDF file

// 3. Confirm upload with base64
POST /protocols/{protocol_id}/confirm-upload { pdf_bytes_base64 }
```

**Key Page Objects:**
- Login page: `/login`
- Protocol upload trigger: `/protocols` → "Upload Protocol" button
- Protocol list: `/protocols`
- Review page: `/reviews/:batchId`
- Results/extraction view: Protocol detail or Review page

---

### 6. IMPORTANT CONFIGURATION

**Environment Variables:**
- `VITE_API_URL`: API base URL (defaults to `http://localhost:8000`)
- For production deployment: Set to `https://api-1074735463071.europe-west4.run.app`

**App Name:** GemmaCrit

All authenticated requests use the `fetchApi()` wrapper which automatically includes the Bearer token from localStorage.

   - Accepts PDF files only (`accept="application/pdf"`)
   - Validates file type: must be `application/pdf`
   - Validates file size: max 50MB
   - Supports drag-and-drop or file picker
   - Shows file preview with name and size

3. **Upload Steps** (useUploadProtocol hook):
   - **Step 1:** POST `/protocols/upload` with metadata
     ```json
     {
       "filename": "file.name",
       "content_type": "application/pdf",
       "file_size_bytes": 12345
     }
     ```
     - Response: `{ protocol_id, upload_url, gcs_path }`
   
   - **Step 2:** PUT file directly to GCS using signed URL
     - Uses `fetch(uploadUrl, { method: 'PUT', body: file })`
     - Headers: `Content-Type: application/pdf`
   
   - **Step 3:** POST `/protocols/{protocol_id}/confirm-upload` with base64 encoded PDF
     ```json
     {
       "pdf_bytes_base64": "base64_encoded_pdf"
     }
     ```
     - Triggers quality scoring and extraction pipeline

4. **Processing States:**
   After upload, protocol goes through states:
   - `uploaded` → Initial state
   - `extracting` → PDF text/data extraction in progress
   - `extraction_failed` → Extraction error (can retry)
   - `grounding` → Entity grounding/linking in progress
   - `grounding_failed` → Grounding error (can retry)
   - `pending_review` → Ready for human review
   - `complete` → All processing done
   - `dead_letter` → Unrecoverable error (can retry)
   - `archived` → Hidden from default list

---

### 3. PROCESSING RESULTS DISPLAY

**Main Results Routes:**

1. **Protocol List Page (`/protocols`):**
   - Shows all uploaded protocols in table
   - Displays: Title, Status, Page Count, Quality Score, Upload Time
   - Filter by status or show archived
   - Status badges with color coding
   - Quality score indicator (0-100% progress bar)
   - Actions: Retry (for failed), Archive, Click to detail view

2. **Protocol Detail Page (`/protocols/:id`):**
   - Shows protocol metadata
   - Status and quality score
   - Timeline of batches/extractions
   - Agreement metrics
   - Button to "Review" (links to review batch)
   - Re-extract option (creates new batch)

3. **Review Queue (`/reviews`):**
   - Lists all review batches pending human review
   - Shows batch status, criteria count, etc.
   - Click to open ReviewPage

4. **Review Page (`/reviews/:batchId`):**
   - **Left panel:** PDF Viewer (PdfViewer.tsx) 
     - Shows original protocol PDF with page navigation
   
   - **Right panel:** Extracted criteria and entities
     - Tabs: "Criteria" and "Entities"
     - Each criterion shows:
       - Extracted text
       - Confidence score
       - Review status (approved/rejected)
       - Action buttons (Approve/Reject/Modify)
     - Entities grouped by criteria_id
   
   - **Search & Filter:**
     - Text search across criteria
     - Filter by status (pending/approved/rejected)
     - Filter by type
     - Filter by confidence level
   
   - **Audit Trail:**
     - Shows who reviewed what and when
     - Collapsible audit history panel

5. **Criteria Spreadsheet (`/criteria`):**
   - Spreadsheet view of all criteria across all batches
   - Sortable columns
   - Inline editing

6. **Entity List (`/entities/:batchId`):**
   - Lists extracted entities for a batch
   - Shows entity type and mapped values
   - Can approve/modify/reject individual entities

---

### 4. KEY API ENDPOINTS

**Authentication:**
- `POST /auth/login?popup=1` - OAuth popup login
- `POST /auth/dev-login` - Dev login

**Protocols:**
- `GET /protocols?page=1&page_size=20&status=X` - List protocols
- `GET /protocols/:id` - Get protocol detail
- `POST /protocols/upload` - Get signed upload URL
- `PUT {upload_url}` - Upload file to GCS (external)
- `POST /protocols/:id/confirm-upload` - Confirm upload and trigger processing
- `POST /protocols/:id/retry` - Retry failed protocol
- `POST /protocols/:id/re-extract` - Re-extract (new batch)
- `POST /protocols/:id/archive` - Archive protocol

**Reviews:**
- `GET /batches?page=1&page_size=X` - List review batches
- `GET /batches/:batchId/criteria` - Get criteria for batch
- `POST /criteria/:criterionId/review` - Submit criterion review
- `POST /entities/:entityId/action` - Review entity

---

### 5. PLAYWRIGHT E2E TESTING TIPS

**Login Flow for Tests:**
```javascript
// Option 1: Use dev login (faster)
await page.request.post('${API_URL}/auth/dev-login')
// Extract token from response and set in localStorage

// Option 2: Simulate OAuth popup flow
// Mock the window.postMessage from auth popup
await page.evaluate((token, user) => {
  window.dispatchEvent(new MessageEvent('message', {
    data: { access_token: token, user: user },
    origin: new URL(API_URL).origin
  }))
}, token, user)
```

**Upload Flow for Tests:**
```javascript
// 1. Get upload URL
POST /protocols/upload { filename, content_type, file_size_bytes }

// 2. Upload to GCS
PUT {upload_url} with PDF file

// 3. Confirm upload with base64
POST /protocols/{protocol_id}/confirm-upload { pdf_bytes_base64 }
```

**Key Page Objects:**
- Login page: `/login`
- Protocol upload trigger: `/protocols` → "Upload Protocol" button
- Protocol list: `/protocols`
- Review page: `/reviews/:batchId`
- Results/extraction view: Protocol detail or Review page

---

### 6. IMPORTANT CONFIGURATION

**Environment Variables:**
- `VITE_API_URL`: API base URL (defaults to `http://localhost:8000`)
- For production deployment: Set to `https://api-1074735463071.europe-west4.run.app`

**App Name:** GemmaCrit

All authenticated requests use the `fetchApi()` wrapper which automatically includes the Bearer token from localStorage.

"""FastAPI router for Google OAuth authentication and JWT management.

Provides endpoints for:
- GET /auth/login: Redirect to Google OAuth
- GET /auth/callback: Handle OAuth callback and issue JWT
- GET /auth/me: Get current user info from JWT
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import os
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from typing import Any, Dict

import jwt
from authlib.integrations.starlette_client import OAuth
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Request
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel
from shared.models import User
from sqlmodel import Session, select

from api_service.dependencies import get_current_user, get_db

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

router = APIRouter(prefix="/auth", tags=["auth"])

# Configure OAuth client
oauth = OAuth()
oauth.register(
    name="google",
    client_id=os.getenv("GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID"),
    client_secret=os.getenv("GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET"),
    server_metadata_url="https://accounts.google.com/.well-known/openid-configuration",
    client_kwargs={"scope": "openid email profile"},
)

# JWT secret from environment
_DEFAULT_JWT_SECRET = "dev-secret-key-change-in-production"
SECRET_KEY = os.getenv("JWT_SECRET_KEY", _DEFAULT_JWT_SECRET)

# Validate secrets at import time in production
if os.getenv("ENVIRONMENT", "").lower() == "production":
    if SECRET_KEY == _DEFAULT_JWT_SECRET:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "JWT_SECRET_KEY must be set to a secure value in production. "
            "The default dev secret is not allowed."
        )

# Block redirects when OAuth is unconfigured or using a known-deleted client
# (stops Cursor/IDE popups).
DELETED_OAUTH_CLIENT_IDS = frozenset(
    {"1015683497619-c7c8101v1pea8ji7u0a5jh94a8ha6ool.apps.googleusercontent.com"}
)


# --- Response models ---

#!/bin/bash
#
# Rebuild and deploy the API to Cloud Run.
# Run from repo root, or the script will cd to the repo root.
# Usage: make deploy-api  (or  bash scripts/deploy_api.sh)
# Loads environment variables from the repo root .env (GCP_PROJECT_ID, GCP_REGION,
# CONNECTION_NAME, CORS_ORIGINS, GCS_BUCKET_NAME, VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID, etc.).
#
# See DEPLOYMENT.md sections 4.2, 4.4, 4.4b for full details.

set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"

# Load .env first so all deploy variables can come from there
if [ -f "$REPO_ROOT/.env" ]; then
    set -a
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    source "$REPO_ROOT/.env"
    set +a
fi

# Apply defaults only where still unset (env / CLI override .env)
REGION="${REGION:-${GCP_REGION:-europe-west4}}"
PROJECT_ID="${PROJECT_ID:-$GCP_PROJECT_ID}"
CONNECTION_NAME="${CONNECTION_NAME:-}"
GCS_BUCKET_NAME="${GCS_BUCKET_NAME:-}"
VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID="${VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID:-}"
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID="${GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID:-}"
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET="${GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET:-}"
# Use FRONTEND_URL for deploy CORS when set (so .env can keep CORS_ORIGINS for local dev)
CORS_ORIGINS="${FRONTEND_URL:-$CORS_ORIGINS}"

if [ -z "$PROJECT_ID" ]; then
    echo "Error: PROJECT_ID not set. Set GCP_PROJECT_ID in .env or export PROJECT_ID." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Deploy requires these; set in .env or export before running
if [ -z "$CONNECTION_NAME" ]; then
    echo "Error: CONNECTION_NAME not set (Cloud SQL connection name). Set in .env or export." >&2
    exit 1
fi
if [ -z "$CORS_ORIGINS" ]; then
    echo "Error: CORS_ORIGINS not set (frontend URL). Set in .env or export." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Prefer GCS_BUCKET_NAME_PROD for deploy (local .env GCS_BUCKET_NAME may be the cloudbuild bucket)
GCS_BUCKET_NAME="${GCS_BUCKET_NAME_PROD:-${GCS_BUCKET_NAME:-${PROJECT_ID}-api-protocols}}"

if [ -z "$VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID" ]; then
    echo "Error: VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID not set. Set in .env or export." >&2
    exit 1
fi

if [ -z "$GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID" ] || [ -z "$GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET" ]; then
    echo "Warning: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET not set. Google OAuth login will be unavailable." >&2
fi

# Auto-resolve MLflow URL from Cloud Run if not explicitly set
MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI="${MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI:-}"
if [ -z "$MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI" ]; then
    MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=$(gcloud run services describe mlflow \
        --region "$REGION" --project "$PROJECT_ID" \
        --format='value(status.url)' 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI" ]; then
        echo "Auto-resolved MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI: $MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI"
    else
        echo "Warning: No MLflow service found. Tracing will be disabled (protocol processing unaffected)." >&2
    fi
fi

cd "$REPO_ROOT"

echo "Building API image (Cloud Build)..."
gcloud builds submit \
    --project "$PROJECT_ID" \
    --config=cloudbuild-api.yaml \
    --substitutions=_REGION="${REGION}" \
    .

echo "Deploying API to Cloud Run..."
gcloud run deploy api \
    --project "$PROJECT_ID" \
    --image "${REGION}-docker.pkg.dev/${PROJECT_ID}/app-images/api:latest" \
    --region "$REGION" \
    --platform managed \
    --allow-unauthenticated \
    --no-cpu-throttling \
    --add-cloudsql-instances "$CONNECTION_NAME" \
    --startup-probe-path=/health \
    --startup-probe-initial-delay=5 \
    --startup-probe-period=10 \
    --startup-probe-failure-threshold=6 \
    --set-env-vars "^||^ENVIRONMENT=production||GCP_PROJECT_ID=${PROJECT_ID}||GCP_REGION=${REGION}||MODEL_BACKEND=vertex||VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID=${VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID}||GCS_BUCKET_NAME=${GCS_BUCKET_NAME}||USE_LOCAL_STORAGE=0||CORS_ORIGINS=${CORS_ORIGINS}||GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=${GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID}||GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=${GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET}||MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=${MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI}||MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASYNC_TRACE_LOGGING=true" \
    --set-secrets "DATABASE_URL=db-url:latest,SESSION_SECRET=api-session-secret:latest,JWT_SECRET_KEY=api-jwt-secret:latest,OMOP_VOCAB_URL=omop-vocab-url:latest"

# Post-deploy health check
API_URL=$(gcloud run services describe api \
    --region "$REGION" --project "$PROJECT_ID" \
    --format='value(status.url)' 2>/dev/null)

echo "API URL: ${API_URL:-unknown}"

if [ -n "$API_URL" ]; then
    echo "Verifying deployment health..."
    HTTP_STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 30 "${API_URL}/health" 2>/dev/null || echo "000")
    if [ "$HTTP_STATUS" = "200" ]; then
        echo "Health check PASSED (HTTP $HTTP_STATUS)"
    else
        echo "Warning: Health check returned HTTP $HTTP_STATUS (new revision may still be starting)" >&2
    fi
else
    echo "Warning: Could not determine API URL for health check" >&2
fi

"""Unified outbox event handler for ProtocolUploaded events.

Replaces the two-service trigger pattern (extraction_service + grounding_service)
with a single consolidated handler that invokes the full 5-node pipeline:
ingest -> extract -> parse -> ground -> persist

Per user decision (v2.0): "Remove criteria_extracted outbox, retain protocol_uploaded"

The handler is synchronous (called by OutboxProcessor.poll_and_process) and
bridges to the async graph via asyncio.run(). This works without event loop
conflicts because the outbox processor runs handlers in a thread executor
via run_in_executor, so there is no existing event loop in the current thread.

Checkpointing: Each invocation generates a unique thread_id (protocol_id:uuid4)
and stores it in protocol.metadata_ so that retry_from_checkpoint can look it up.
This prevents checkpoint collision when re-extracting the same protocol.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import logging
import os
from typing import Any
from uuid import uuid4

from api_service.storage import engine  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
from shared.exceptions import AuthExpiredError
from shared.models import Protocol
from sqlmodel import Session

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def _cleanup_orphan_traces() -> None:
    """Close stale IN_PROGRESS MLflow traces from previous crashed runs.

    Runs once at module import (service startup). Idempotent -- safe to
    call multiple times. Only closes traces older than 1 hour to avoid
    closing currently-running pipelines.

    Skips when MLflow circuit breaker is open to avoid timeout delays.
    """
    import time as _time

    from shared.resilience import mlflow_is_available

    if not mlflow_is_available():
        return

def handle_protocol_uploaded(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Handle a ProtocolUploaded event by running the full pipeline.

    Constructs the initial PipelineState from the event payload and
    invokes the consolidated 5-node LangGraph workflow via asyncio.run().

    Uses protocol_id as the LangGraph thread_id so that retry_from_checkpoint
    can locate the saved checkpoint by protocol_id alone.

    Replaces both extraction_service.trigger.handle_protocol_uploaded and
    grounding_service.trigger.handle_criteria_extracted from the v1.x
    two-service architecture.

    Args:
        payload: Event payload dict containing protocol_id, file_uri, and title.

    Raises:
        DependencyCheckError: If DB or OMOP is unreachable.
        Exception: Re-raised after logging to let the outbox processor
            mark the event as failed for retry.
    """
    # Pre-flight: verify all infrastructure dependencies are up before
    # spending any Gemini/ToolUniverse API calls.
    _preflight_check()

    # Set MLflow experiment for this worker thread (protocol-processing-YYYYMMDD).
    # Without this, the thread would use default experiment ID 0, which may be deleted.
    _ensure_mlflow()
    # So pipeline spans carry the experiment ID and export works from any thread.
    try:
        import mlflow

        from protocol_processor.tracing import set_pipeline_experiment_id

        exp = mlflow.get_experiment_by_name(_get_experiment_name())
        if exp:
            set_pipeline_experiment_id(exp.experiment_id)
        else:
            set_pipeline_experiment_id(None)
    except Exception:
        logger.debug("Could not set pipeline experiment ID for tracing", exc_info=True)

    protocol_id = payload.get("protocol_id", "unknown")
    logger.info(
        "Handling ProtocolUploaded event for protocol %s (consolidated pipeline)",
        protocol_id,
    )

    try:
        # Generate unique thread_id per pipeline run to prevent checkpoint collision
        # on re-extraction (same protocol_id would resume old completed checkpoint)
        thread_id = f"{protocol_id}:{uuid4()}"

        initial_state: dict[str, Any] = {
            "protocol_id": payload["protocol_id"],
            "file_uri": payload["file_uri"],
            "title": payload["title"],
            "batch_id": None,
            "pdf_bytes": None,
            "extraction_json": None,
            "entities_json": None,
            "grounded_entities_json": None,
            "archived_reviewed_criteria": payload.get("archived_reviewed_criteria"),
            "status": "processing",
            "error": None,
            "errors": [],
        }

        # Store thread_id in protocol metadata for retry_from_checkpoint lookup
        try:
            with Session(engine) as session:
                protocol = session.get(Protocol, protocol_id)
                if protocol:
                    meta = protocol.metadata_ or {}
                    protocol.metadata_ = {
                        **meta,
                        "pipeline_thread_id": thread_id,
                    }
                    session.add(protocol)
                    session.commit()
        except Exception:
            logger.warning(
                "Failed to store pipeline_thread_id for protocol %s",
                protocol_id,
            )

        config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": thread_id}}

        asyncio.run(_run_pipeline(initial_state, config, payload))

        logger.info(
            "Protocol pipeline completed for protocol %s",
            protocol_id,
        )

    except Exception as e:
        logger.exception(
            "Protocol pipeline failed for protocol %s",
            protocol_id,
        )

content.text:
Here's the situation with **MLflow**:

## MLflow Status

**MLflow Cloud Run service exists** at: `https://mlflow-aq2dyw3nxq-ez.a.run.app`

You can access the MLflow UI by navigating to that URL in your browser. However, there's a critical issue:

## The Problem: Wrong MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI

The deployed API has `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://localhost:5001` — this is the **local dev value** from your `.env` file. The deploy script sources `.env` first, and since `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` is already set there, the auto-resolve logic (which would correctly fetch the Cloud Run MLflow URL) gets skipped.

This causes:
1. **All MLflow trace exports fail** (trying to reach localhost:5001 instead of the Cloud Run URL)
2. **urllib3 retries flood the logs** with exponential backoff warnings
3. The pipeline is **still running** (trace attempts confirm LLM nodes are executing) but it's slower because the MLflow retries add overhead

Let me fix the deploy script to override the local `.env` value for MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI, then redeploy.

#!/bin/bash
#
# Rebuild and deploy the API to Cloud Run.
# Run from repo root, or the script will cd to the repo root.
# Usage: make deploy-api  (or  bash scripts/deploy_api.sh)
# Loads environment variables from the repo root .env (GCP_PROJECT_ID, GCP_REGION,
# CONNECTION_NAME, CORS_ORIGINS, GCS_BUCKET_NAME, VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID, etc.).
#
# See DEPLOYMENT.md sections 4.2, 4.4, 4.4b for full details.

set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"

# Load .env first so all deploy variables can come from there
if [ -f "$REPO_ROOT/.env" ]; then
    set -a
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    source "$REPO_ROOT/.env"
    set +a
fi

# Apply defaults only where still unset (env / CLI override .env)
REGION="${REGION:-${GCP_REGION:-europe-west4}}"
PROJECT_ID="${PROJECT_ID:-$GCP_PROJECT_ID}"
CONNECTION_NAME="${CONNECTION_NAME:-}"
GCS_BUCKET_NAME="${GCS_BUCKET_NAME:-}"
VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID="${VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID:-}"
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID="${GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID:-}"
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET="${GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET:-}"
# Use FRONTEND_URL for deploy CORS when set (so .env can keep CORS_ORIGINS for local dev)
CORS_ORIGINS="${FRONTEND_URL:-$CORS_ORIGINS}"

if [ -z "$PROJECT_ID" ]; then
    echo "Error: PROJECT_ID not set. Set GCP_PROJECT_ID in .env or export PROJECT_ID." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Deploy requires these; set in .env or export before running
if [ -z "$CONNECTION_NAME" ]; then
    echo "Error: CONNECTION_NAME not set (Cloud SQL connection name). Set in .env or export." >&2
    exit 1
fi
if [ -z "$CORS_ORIGINS" ]; then
    echo "Error: CORS_ORIGINS not set (frontend URL). Set in .env or export." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Prefer GCS_BUCKET_NAME_PROD for deploy (local .env GCS_BUCKET_NAME may be the cloudbuild bucket)
GCS_BUCKET_NAME="${GCS_BUCKET_NAME_PROD:-${GCS_BUCKET_NAME:-${PROJECT_ID}-api-protocols}}"

if [ -z "$VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID" ]; then
    echo "Error: VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID not set. Set in .env or export." >&2
    exit 1
fi

if [ -z "$GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID" ] || [ -z "$GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET" ]; then
    echo "Warning: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET not set. Google OAuth login will be unavailable." >&2
fi

# Auto-resolve MLflow URL from Cloud Run if not explicitly set
MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI="${MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI:-}"
if [ -z "$MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI" ]; then
    MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=$(gcloud run services describe mlflow \
        --region "$REGION" --project "$PROJECT_ID" \
        --format='value(status.url)' 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI" ]; then
        echo "Auto-resolved MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI: $MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI"
    else
        echo "Warning: No MLflow service found. Tracing will be disabled (protocol processing unaffected)." >&2
    fi
fi

cd "$REPO_ROOT"

echo "Building API image (Cloud Build)..."
gcloud builds submit \
    --project "$PROJECT_ID" \
    --config=cloudbuild-api.yaml \
    --substitutions=_REGION="${REGION}" \
    .

echo "Deploying API to Cloud Run..."
gcloud run deploy api \
    --project "$PROJECT_ID" \
    --image "${REGION}-docker.pkg.dev/${PROJECT_ID}/app-images/api:latest" \
    --region "$REGION" \
    --platform managed \
    --allow-unauthenticated \
    --no-cpu-throttling \
    --add-cloudsql-instances "$CONNECTION_NAME" \
    --startup-probe=httpGet.path=/health,initialDelaySeconds=5,periodSeconds=10,failureThreshold=6 \
    --set-env-vars "^||^ENVIRONMENT=production||GCP_PROJECT_ID=${PROJECT_ID}||GCP_REGION=${REGION}||MODEL_BACKEND=vertex||VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID=${VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID}||GCS_BUCKET_NAME=${GCS_BUCKET_NAME}||USE_LOCAL_STORAGE=0||CORS_ORIGINS=${CORS_ORIGINS}||GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=${GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID}||GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=${GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET}||MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=${MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI}||MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASYNC_TRACE_LOGGING=true" \
    --set-secrets "DATABASE_URL=db-url:latest,SESSION_SECRET=api-session-secret:latest,JWT_SECRET_KEY=api-jwt-secret:latest,OMOP_VOCAB_URL=omop-vocab-url:latest"

# Post-deploy health check
API_URL=$(gcloud run services describe api \
    --region "$REGION" --project "$PROJECT_ID" \
    --format='value(status.url)' 2>/dev/null)

echo "API URL: ${API_URL:-unknown}"

if [ -n "$API_URL" ]; then
    echo "Verifying deployment health..."
    HTTP_STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 30 "${API_URL}/health" 2>/dev/null || echo "000")
    if [ "$HTTP_STATUS" = "200" ]; then
        echo "Health check PASSED (HTTP $HTTP_STATUS)"
    else
        echo "Warning: Health check returned HTTP $HTTP_STATUS (new revision may still be starting)" >&2
    fi
else
    echo "Warning: Could not determine API URL for health check" >&2
fi
